    57	    /// Steps 3–6. The walk holds identities, never images: each child scan
    58	    /// streams `PAGE` rows per seek, and every write rereads its row current.
    59	    fn reference_closure(&mut self, root_table: &str, root: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    60	        let schema = self.schema;
    61	        let mut seen: BTreeSet<(String, String)> = BTreeSet::from([(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned())]);
    62	        // (Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.)
    63	        let mut visits: Vec<(String, Value)> = vec![(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.clone())];
    64	        // 3. Close over cascades, breadth first. Every reached row's referencing groups must be held on a device.
    65	        let mut next = 0;
    66	        while next < visits.len() {
    67	            let (table, id) = visits[next].clone();
    68	            next += 1;
    69	            for r in schema.referencing(&table) {
    70	                if self.device && !through_reference(&r) { self.prove_reference_held(&r, &id)?; }
    71	                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
    72	                self.each_child(&r, &id, true, &mut |_, child| {
    73	                    if seen.insert((r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned())) { visits.push((r.child.to_owned(), child)); }
    74	                    Ok(true)
    75	                })?;
    76	            }
    77	        }
    78	        // 4. Restrict: every probe runs, streaming past closure rows (the root
    79	        // included) to the first outside witness; the first occupied reference
    80	        // in schema order is reported. One reference's probes visit each closure
    81	        // row at most once, plus one witness per probe (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
    82	        let mut occupied: Option<(String, String, String)> = None;
    83	        for (table, id) in &visits {
    84	            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
    85	                if r.action != OnDelete::Restrict || through_reference(&r) { continue; }
    86	                let mut outside = false;
    87	                self.each_child(&r, id, false, &mut |_, child| {
    88	                    outside = !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned()));
    89	                    Ok(!outside)
    90	                })?;
    91	                let candidate = (r.child.to_owned(), r.column.to_owned(), table.clone());
    92	                if outside && occupied.as_ref().is_none_or(|o| candidate < *o) { occupied = Some(candidate); }
    93	            }
    94	        }
    95	        if let Some((child, column, parent)) = occupied {
    96	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    97	            self.refusing_clause(&child, &format!("{column}: {parent} (on delete restrict)"));
    98	            let via = if parent == root_table { String::new() } else { format!(", through a {parent} row this delete cascades to") };
    99	            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED", message: format!("{root_table} at {} is still referenced through {child}.{column} (on delete restrict){via}; delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)", self.statement_site) });
   100	        }
   101	        // A cascaded row can itself have a physically retained read-through
   102	        // child. Decide that blocker before set-null writes begin, so expiry
   103	        // can retain this root and continue without relying on transaction
   104	        // rollback to undo a partial closure.
   105	        for (table, id) in visits.iter().skip(1) {
   106	            if self.physical_children_outside(table, id, &seen)? {
   107	                return Err(self.parent_has_children(table));
   108	            }
   109	        }
   110	        // 5. Set null outside the closure. Each group is gathered whole before
   111	        // any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling that shares the
   112	        // reference's index and move it behind a page cursor. Each row is then
   113	        // reread current before its write.
   114	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — gather, then clear: no row moves out of a walk it has not finished.
   115	        for (table, id) in &visits {
   116	            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
   117	                if r.action != OnDelete::SetNull { continue; }
   118	                let mut group: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   119	                self.each_child(&r, id, true, &mut |_, child| {
   120	                    let child = child.as_str()?.to_owned();
   121	                    if !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.clone())) { group.push(child); }
   122	                    Ok(true)
   123	                })?;
   124	                for child in group {
   125	                    let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, r.child, &child))?;
   126	                    if let Some(current) = current.filter(|row| row.field(r.column).is_ok_and(|v| v == id)) {
   127	                        self.clear_reference(r.child, r.column, current)?;
   128	                    }
   129	                }
   130	            }
   131	        }
   132	        // 6. Delete the closure, children first, each from its current image.
   133	        let reached: Vec<(String, String)> = visits[1..].iter().map(|(t, id)| Ok((t.clone(), id.as_str()?.to_owned()))).collect::<Result<_, RuntimeError>>()?;
   134	        drop(visits);
   135	        for (table, id) in deletion_order(schema, &reached) {
   136	            let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &table, &id))?;
   137	            let Some(current) = current else { continue };
   138	            self.delete_reached(&table, current)?;
   139	        }
   140	        Ok(())
   141	    }

   143	    /// Streams the ids of the live rows referencing `id` through `r` to
   144	    /// `visit`, through its index, until `visit` answers false. A capped walk
   145	    /// (cascade, set null) reads `PAGE` rows per seek and holds at most the
   146	    /// reference's cap; a restrict probe reads one row per seek, so it examines
   147	    /// nothing past its witness. Images are dropped before `visit` runs. Seeks
   148	    /// start at the live suffix, so an expired backlog is never visited.
   149	    fn each_child(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value, capped: bool, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Self, Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   150	        let schema = self.schema;
   151	        let index = schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();

   243	/// discoveries first.
   244	fn deletion_order(schema: &crate::schema::Schema, reached: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
   245	    let tables: Vec<&str> = {
   246	        let mut seen = Vec::new();
   247	        for (table, _) in reached { if !seen.contains(&table.as_str()) { seen.push(table.as_str()); } }

   249	    };

   251	    // (its cascade parents and its `read through` parent; LLP 3000.039 §3).
   252	    let mut edges: Vec<(&str, &str)> = Vec::new();

   262	        let position = remaining.iter().position(|t| !remaining.iter().any(|other| other != t && edges.contains(&(*other, *t))))

   267	    for table in order {
   268	        out.extend(reached.iter().rev().filter(|(t, _)| t == table).cloned());

   263	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   264	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &patch, false)?;
   265	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   266	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   267	        })? else {
   268	            return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]));
   269	        };
   270	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].sync.is_none() { return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])); }
   271	        let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   272	            && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   273	        let patch = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, patch, readable)?;
   274	        let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &patch, readable)?;
   275	        self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &patch, copy)
   276	    }
   277	
   278	    pub(super) fn upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   279	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   280	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   281	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   282	            ));
   283	        }
   284	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   285	            runner.upsert_attempt(table_name, key, row)
   286	        })
   287	    }
   288	
   289	    fn upsert_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   290	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   291	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &row, false)?;
   292	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &row)?;
   293	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &row)?;
   294	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   295	        if row.field("id")?.as_str()? != id {
   296	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} upsert row id must equal its key")));
   297	        }
   298	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &row, true)?;
   299	        match self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   300	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   301	        })? {
   302	            Some(old) => {
   303	                let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   304	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   305	                let row = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, row, readable)?;
   306	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — an existing row receives a patch; omitted columns keep their values.
   307	                let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &row, readable)?;
   308	                self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &row, copy)
   309	            }
   310	            None if self.device && !self.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])? =>
   311	            {
   312	                Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]))
   313	            }
   314	            None => self.insert_upsert(table_name, "byId", row),
   315	        }
   316	    }
   317	
   318	    pub(super) fn insert_upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, addressed_index: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   319	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   320	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#5 — trusted fixture imports preserve the constraint layer.
   321	        if self.context.is_system() {
   322	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|error| match error {
   323	                RuntimeError::Input(message) => RuntimeError::Constraint(message),
   324	                other => other,
   325	            });
   326	        }
   327	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].through.is_some() {
   328	            // A read-through child's insert arm keeps the hidden-target word for every authority refusal.
   329	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|e| match e {
   330	                RuntimeError::Rule {..} | RuntimeError::Input(_) => self.no_write_target(), other => other,
   331	            });
   332	        }
   333	        match self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()) {
   334	            Err(RuntimeError::Input(_)) => Err(self.no_write_target()),
   335	            result => result,
   336	        }
   337	    }
   338	
   339	    fn replace(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   340	        self.authorize_update_fields(table_name, &old, &new, patch, readable)?;
   341	        self.replace_authorized(table_name, old, new, readable, patch, copy)
   342	    }
   343	
   344	    /// `copy` is the merged image's lawful price, charged again for an engine slot copy.
   345	    pub(super) fn replace_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   346	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
   347	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, patch, false)?;
   348	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, patch)?;
   349	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, patch)?;
   350	        self.authorize_fields(table_name, &old, patch)?;
   351	        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   352	        for path in definition.columns.keys().filter(|field| {
   353	            definition.engine_field(field) && field.as_str() != crate::schema::through::DEADLINE
   354	        }) {
   355	            if old.field(path).ok() != new.field(path).ok() {
   356	                return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_RECORDED_FIELD", message: format!("engine replacement changed stored attribution at {table_name}.{path} (guide maintains)") } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   357	            }
   358	        }
   359	        let mut new = new;
   360	        self.schema.tables[table_name].recompute_deadline(&mut new)?;
   361	        // @ref LLP 3000.017#2.2 — extending life re-admits the new image.
   362	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].stamp_ephemeral(&mut new, self.context.now.unwrap_or(0))?
   363	            && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &new)? {
   364	            return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.into(), effect: Effect::Update } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   365	        }
   366	        let new = self.with_asset_facts(table_name, new, Some(&old), (!readable).then_some(patch))?;
   367	        if let Err(error) = super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str())) { return Err(if readable { error } else { self.no_write_target() }); }
   368	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &new, Effect::Update)?;
   369	        let new = self.prepare_event_slots(table_name, Some(&old), new, copy)?;
   370	        // A predicting device keeps another owner's omitted private field as an omission.
   371	        super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str()))?;
   372	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   373	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   374	            runner.tx.put(table_name, table, &new, Some(&old))
   375	        })?;
   376	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), Some(&new), entries)?;
   377	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), Some(&new), Origin::Source)
   378	    }
   379	
   380	    pub(super) fn delete(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   381	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   382	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   383	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   384	            ));
   385	        }
   386	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| runner.delete_attempt(table_name, id))
   387	    }
   388	
   389	    fn delete_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   390	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   391	        self.refuse_receipt_scope_delete(table_name)?;
   392	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   393	        self.reserve_write_rules(table, &[Effect::Read, Effect::Delete])?;
   394	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — delete prepays hidden contribution work before fetching its old image, with the same attempt lifetime as update.
   395	        self.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
   396	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   397	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   398	        })? else {
   399	            return Err(RuntimeError::Require { site: Some(self.statement_site.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".to_owned(), message: None });
   400	        };
   401	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — a delete that consults referencing rows needs read authority on its row first.
   402	        let readable =
   403	            !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)? && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   404	        if (self.schema.children(table_name).next().is_some() || self.schema.is_referenced(table_name)) && !readable
   405	        {
   406	            self.refusing_clause(table_name, "read rule");
   407	            return Err(self.no_write_target());
   408	        }
   409	        if !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Delete, None, &old)? {
   410	            return Err(if readable {
   411	                RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.to_owned(), effect: Effect::Delete }
   412	            } else { self.no_write_target() });
   413	        }
   414	        self.delete_authorized(table_name, old)
   415	    }
   416	
   417	    pub(super) fn delete_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   418	        let old = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   419	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, &old)?;
   420	            // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — the actions may have changed the root (a maintained column mirrored from its children): remove its current image.
   421	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   422	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, &id))?.unwrap_or(old)
   423	        } else { old };
   424	        self.delete_row(table_name, old)
   425	    }
   426	
   427	    /// A delete's own removal of one row, its rules already decided: receipt
   428	    /// membership, the read-through child probe, constraints, maintains and
   429	    /// the partition event. A referential cascade removes each row this way.
   430	    pub(super) fn delete_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   431	        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   432	        self.receipt_member_removed(table_name, &old)?;
   433	        self.refuse_live_children(table_name,old.field("id")?)?;
   434	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &old, Effect::Delete)?;
   435	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   436	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, &old)
   437	        })?;
   438	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), None, entries)?;
   439	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), None, Origin::Source)
   440	    }
   441	
   442	    /// Remove a row the engine itself retires (an expired one): no rule and
   443	    /// no constraint stands between the engine and its own sweep, while
   444	    /// aggregates and partition events apply as for any delete.
   445	    pub(super) fn remove(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   446	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   447	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   448	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   449	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, old)
   450	        })?;
   451	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(old), None, entries)?;
   452	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(old), None, Origin::Source)
   453	    }
   454	
   455	    /// Physically retire one row whose upper lifetime ended. Expiry bypasses
   456	    /// the root's authored delete rule and constraints, but it does not bypass
   457	    /// the schema's declared effects on rows that reference the root. A
   458	    /// read-through child still retains the expired parent physically.
   459	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — expiry cleanup runs the same closure/restrict/set-null actions as an authored delete.
   460	    pub(super) fn retire_expired_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   461	        if self.physical_children(table_name, old.field("id")?)? { return Ok(false); }
   462	        let current = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   463	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, old)?;
   464	            // A cascade may maintain a column on the root; delete its current
   465	            // physical image so index and cap entries match what is stored.
   466	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?;
   467	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))?
   468	                .unwrap_or_else(|| old.clone())
   469	        } else {
   470	            old.clone()
   471	        };
   472	        self.remove(table_name, &current)?;
   473	        Ok(true)
   474	    }
   475	
   476	    /// At a program commit's end, retire every synced row the commit changed
   477	    /// and every row it inserted whose lifetime has already ended: its final
   478	    /// image was never live at a commit boundary, so it leaves no row for a
   479	    /// later sweep to announce. Inside the commit the
   480	    /// row existed as written (an insert-then-update still works). Engine
   481	    /// bookkeeping, unmetered: the device's prediction does not do it, and
   482	    /// the program's metering is already recorded. Its work, returned, stays
   483	    /// linear in the rows retired: each aggregate row takes one net change
   484	    /// and each audience key is scanned for a live row once. Seeds and loads
   485	    /// keep their rows for the sweep.
   486	    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — a row whose lifetime ended by its own commit's end never exists at a commit boundary.
   487	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   488	    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_births(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   489	        let Some(now) = self.context.now else { return Ok(Default::default());
   490	        };
   491	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#3 — an expired final image never grants a new recipient the row's id.
   492	        // A row that existed before the commit and ends it already expired is
   493	        // retired too: accounted from the partitions it was in at the commit's
   494	        // start, it revokes there and announces nothing to a partition it only
   495	        // entered with its expiring image.
   496	        let mut changed: Vec<(String, String)> = self.born_rows.keys()
   497	            .chain(self.touched_rows.keys())
   498	            .filter(|(table, _)| self.schema.table(table).is_some_and(|t| t.is_expiring()))
   499	            .cloned().collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>().into_iter().collect();
   500	        if changed.is_empty() {
   501	            return Ok(Default::default());
   502	        }
   503	        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
   504	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   505	        changed.sort_by_key(|(name,id)| {
   506	            (std::cmp::Reverse(order.iter().position(|n| n == name)),id.clone(),
   507	            )
   508	        });
   509	        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort));
   510	        self.retiring = Some(Default::default());
   511	        let retired = changed.iter().try_for_each(|(table_name, id)| {
   512	            let Some(row) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))? else { return Ok(());
   513	            };
   514	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   515	            if table.expired(&row, now) { self.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row).map(|_| ()) } else { Ok(()) }
   516	        });
   517	        let aggregates = self.retiring.take().map(|retiring| retiring.aggregates).unwrap_or_default();
   518	        let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));
   519	        let work = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used;
   520	        retired.map(|()| work)
   521	    }
   522	
   523	    /// A column with a declared default takes it when the written row leaves
   524	    /// it out, before validation and before the asset facts, so the row the
   525	    /// rules and the constraints see is the complete one.
   526	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — omitted defaults use the clock and viewer of the host running the insert.
   527	    pub(super) fn with_defaults(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<Supplied, RuntimeError> {
   528	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   529	        if !table.defaults.keys().any(|name| {
   530	            row.as_object().is_ok_and(|fields| !fields.contains_key(name))
   531	        }) {
   532	            return Ok(row);
   533	        }
   534	        let row = row.defaults(table,self.context.now.ok_or_else(||RuntimeError::Input("write clock is not pinned".into()))?,&self.context.viewer)?;
   535	        self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?;
   536	        Ok(row)
   537	    }
   538	
   539	    /// An `image`/`video` column names an upload by id; the row carries the
   540	    /// facts the server established about it (type, bytes, dimensions,
   541	    /// duration), never the client's word for them. The upload must be the
   542	    /// writer's own and of the column's kind and size. The system principal
   543	    /// may name an asset that was never uploaded: a fixture's placeholder,
   544	    /// metadata only, never served.
   545	    // Web stores hold received asset facts, never the authoritative upload ledger.
   546	    #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
   547	    fn with_asset_facts(&mut self, _table_name: &str, row: Value, _old: Option<&Value>, _hidden_patch: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
   548	        Ok(row)
   549	    }
   550	
   551	    pub(super) fn refuse_upsert_owned(&self, table: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   552	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Insert)?;
   553	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Update)
   554	    }
   555	
   556	    /// Programs never write a maintained target; the engine does.
   557	    pub(super) fn refuse_engine_owned(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   558	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — pending member changes cannot rewrite settled requirements.
   559	        if self.device && effect != Effect::Insert && self.schema.receipts.iter().any(|f| f.members == table || f.runs == table) {
   560	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt membership changes and progress queue until settlement".into()));
   561	        }
   562	        self.refuse_receipt_table(table)?;
   563	        self.refuse_condition_write()?;
   564	        self.refuse_timeline_write(table, effect)?;
   565	        self.schema.refuse_private(table)?;
   566	        if self.schema.maintain_for(table).is_some() {
   567	            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table} is a maintained aggregate; write its source rows instead")));
   568	        }
   569	        Ok(())
   570	    }
   571	
   572	    fn check_constraints(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: &Value, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   573	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   574	        let id = new.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   575	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.1 — an action's own write consults no rule: probing the child's read rule would draw the shared allowance only where a child exists.
   576	        let readable = match old { Some(old) if effect == Effect::Update && !self.engine_action => {
   577	                !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, old)?
   578	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, old)?
   579	            }
   580	            _ => true };
   581	        if effect != Effect::Delete {
   582	            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| index.unique) {
   583	                // byId can only return this id (already checked on insert).
   584	                // An unchanged admitted unique key cannot acquire a collision.
   585	                if name == "byId" { continue; }
   586	                let key = index_values(index, new);
   587	                if old.is_some_and(|old| index_values(index, old) == key) { continue; }
   588	                if key.iter().any(|value| *value == Value::Null) {
   589	                    continue;
   590	                }
   591	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — holding the target does not cover a different unique population.
   592	                if self.device && effect == Effect::Update && !self.device_work(|runner| {
   593	                        runner.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, name, &key)
   594	                    })? {
   595	                    return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, name, &key));
   596	                }
   597	                if let Some(existing) = self.collision_lookup(table_name, name, index, &key, Some(&id), effect)
   598	                    .map_err(|error| {
   599	                        if !readable && matches!(error, RuntimeError::Rule { .. }) { self.no_write_target() } else { error
   600	                        }
   601	                    })?
   602	                    && existing.field("id")?.as_str()? != id
   603	                {
   604	                    self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, new, &index.columns(), effect == Effect::Insert)?;
   605	                    if effect == Effect::Update && !readable {
   606	                        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   607	                        self.refusing_clause(table_name, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")));
   608	                        return Err(self.no_write_target());
   609	                    }
   610	                    // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.9 — the dev log names the `unique` line that refused (wave 3 I3).
   611	                    self.refusing_clause(table_name, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")));
   612	                    let declared=index.components.iter().map(|part| match part {
   613	                        crate::schema::IndexComponent::Calendar(k) if k.function=="bucket" => format!("bucket({}, {}{})",k.column,k.millis,if k.offset==0 {String::new()} else {format!(", {}",k.offset)}),
   614	                        crate::schema::IndexComponent::Calendar(k)=>format!("{}({}{})",k.function,k.column,if k.offset==0 {String::new()} else {format!(", {}",k.offset)}),
   615	                        _=>part.key_name().cloned().unwrap_or_else(||"<key>".into()),
   616	                    }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
   617	                    let detail = format!("{table_name}: unique {declared} already has a row where {declared} = {}", key.iter().map(describe).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "));
   618	                    if let Some(refusal) = self.schema.unique_refusals.get(table_name).and_then(|indexes| indexes.get(name)) {
   619	                        return Err(RuntimeError::NamedConstraint { code: refusal.code.clone(), message: refusal.message.clone(), detail });
   620	                    }
   621	                    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#8 — the public code names uniqueness;
   622	                    // diagnostics use declared columns, never planner index names.
   623	                    return Err(RuntimeError::NamedConstraint { code: "E_UNIQUE".into(), message: detail.clone(), detail });
   624	                }
   625	            }
   626	        }
   627	        for constraint in &table.constraints {
   628	            match constraint {
   629	                Constraint::Capabilities(_) | Constraint::Recorded | Constraint::Unique { .. } | Constraint::Text { .. } | Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { .. } => {}
   630	                Constraint::AppendOnly => {

   750	    fn collision_lookup(&mut self, table: &str, name: &str, index: &crate::schema::Index, key: &[Value], except: Option<&str>, effect: Effect) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
   751	        let probes = super::rules::rule_probes(&self.schema.tables[table].rules.read);
   752	        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes)], |runner, allowance| {
   753	            let found = if runner.schema.tables[table].not_before.is_some() {
   754	                runner.lookup_write_occupant(table, name, index, key)?
   755	            } else {
   756	                runner.live_lookup(allowance, table, name, index, key, #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] None)?
   757	            };
   758	            if let Some(row) = &found && Some(row.field("id")?.as_str()?) != except {
   759	                runner.observe_sequence_columns(table, row, &index.columns(), effect == Effect::Insert)?;
   760	                runner.visible_collision(table, row, effect, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")))?;
   761	            }

   771	        effect: Effect,
   772	        clause: &str,

   783	    /// `after insert <- exists t[...]` holds for every row inserted this
   784	    /// transaction; checked once the program has run.
   785	    pub(super) fn check_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   786	        let inserted = std::mem::take(&mut self.inserted);
   787	        for (table_name, row) in &inserted {
   788	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   789	            for constraint in &table.constraints {
   790	                let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key } = constraint else { continue;
   791	                };
   792	                let refusal = || {
   793	                    RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("inserting into {table_name} requires a matching row in {target} by the end of the mutation"))
   794	                };
   795	                let has_references = key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some());
   796	                let key: Vec<Value> = if has_references {
   797	                    // Preserve the structural target probe, but authorize each
   798	                    // live row supplying its key before it can confer authority.
   799	                    let rule = crate::schema::RuleExpr::Exists { table: target.clone(), index: index.clone(), key: key.clone(), equalities: vec![], provenance: crate::ir::KeyProvenance::Shape };
   800	                    for term in key { if let crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) = term { self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field); } }
   801	                    self.final_reference_key(table_name, &rule, row)?.ok_or_else(refusal)?
   802	                } else { key
   803	                    .iter()
   804	                    .map(|term| match term {
   805	                        crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::NextField(field) => {
   806	                            // This inserted image owns a provisional ordinal even if no expression read it.
   807	                            self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field);
   808	                            row.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
   809	                        }
   810	                            crate::schema::RuleTerm::Viewer => {
   811	                                Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone())
   812	                            }
   813	                            crate::schema::RuleTerm::Literal(value) => value.clone(),
   814	                        crate::schema::RuleTerm::OldField(_) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | crate::schema::RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } => Value::Null,
   815	                    })
   816	                    .collect() };
   817	                self.read_tables.insert(target.clone());
   818	                self.observe_sequence_selection(target, index, &key)?;
   819	                let definition = self.schema.table(target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing {target}")))?;
   820	                let target_index = definition.index(index).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing {target}.{index}")))?;
   821	                let found = match self.lookup_stored(target, index, target_index, &key, true)? {
   822	                    Some(row) => self.live_aggregate(target, row)?,
   823	                    None => None,
   824	                };

   826	                    && !self.witness_covered(target, index, &key, row)? {
   827	                    self.unknown_fact(target, index, &key, "after insert");
   828	                    return Err(refusal());
   829	                }

   831	                    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — a final-exists miss needs the same readable, fully held group proof as upsert absence; a local hit needs no absence proof.
   832	                    // Budget spent only while establishing device coverage is the device's
   833	                    // uncertainty, not the write's: the server needs no such proof.
   834	                    let proven = self.device && match self.upsert_absence_proven(target, index, &key) {
   835	                        Ok(proven) => proven,
   836	                        Err(RuntimeError::Bound { .. }) => false,
   837	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   838	                    };

   848	            }
   849	        }
   850	        self.inserted = inserted;
   851	        Ok(())
   852	    }

   854	    fn contribution_heap(&self, table: &Table) -> u64 {
   855	        table.indexes.values().fold(0, |bytes: u64, index| match index.components.first() {
   856	            Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) => bytes.saturating_add(
   857	                super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.target]).saturating_mul(16)),
   858	            _ => bytes,
   859	        })
   860	    }
   861	
   862	    fn charge_source_indexes(&mut self, table: &Table, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>, mut entries: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   863	        for index in table.indexes.values() {
   864	            if let Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() {
   865	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps() * (u64::from(old.is_some()) + u64::from(new.is_some())))?;
   866	            }
   867	        }
   868	        if self.maintain_prepaid {
   869	            let id = old.or(new).expect("source image").field("id")?.as_str()?;
   870	            for index in table.indexes.values() {
   871	                if matches!(index.components.first(), Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(_))) {
   872	                    let before = old.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   873	                    let after = new.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   874	                    let changed = before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)).count() + after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)).count();
   875	                    entries = entries.saturating_sub(changed as u64);
   876	                }
   877	            }
   878	        }
   879	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   880	        Ok(())
   881	    }

   883	    /// The shared tail of every physical row change: creation facts, the
   884	    /// write meter, maintained aggregates, and the partition events.
   885	    pub(super) fn row_changed(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>, origin: Origin) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   886	        if old.is_some() && new.is_none() { self.timeline_purge_charge(table_name)?; }
   887	        if self.schema.visible(table_name) { self.written_tables.insert(table_name.to_owned()); }
   888	        if origin == Origin::Source {
   889	            for m in self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m|m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k|k.table == table_name)) {
   890	                self.written_tables.insert(m.target.clone());
   891	            }
   892	            for m in self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m|m.source == table_name) {
   893	                if let Some(owner) = &m.private { self.written_tables.insert(owner.table.clone()); }
   894	                if m.row_key.is_some() { self.written_tables.insert(m.target.clone()); }
   895	            }
   896	        }
   897	        self.rows_written += 1;
   898	        if origin == Origin::Maintained { self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::RowsWritten, 1)?; }
   899	        else { self.meter.charge(MeterKind::RowsWritten, 1)?; }
   900	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   901	        // Final-exists obligations retain immutable successful-insert images.
   902	        // Current creation facts have separate per-row ownership, so updates
   903	        // and deletes remove only that row's contributions in O(index count).
   904	        let id = old.or(new).expect("a row change has an image").field("id")?.as_str()?;
   905	        let owner = (table_name.to_owned(), id.to_owned());
   906	        if self.device && new.is_some() { self.provisional_rows.insert(owner.clone()); }
   907	        let previous = self.created_rows.remove(&owner);
   908	        let was_created = previous.is_some() || old.is_none();
   909	        if let Some(keys) = previous {
   910	            for key in keys {
   911	                if let Some(count) = self.created.get_mut(&key) {
   912	                    *count -= 1;
   913	                    if *count == 0 { self.created.remove(&key); }
   914	                }
   915	            }
   916	        }
   917	        if old.is_none() {
   918	            if let Some(row) = new { self.inserted.push((table_name.to_owned(), row.clone())); }
   919	        }
   920	        if was_created {
   921	            if let Some(row) = new {
   922	                let keys: Vec<_> = table.indexes.iter().map(|(name, index)| {
   923	                        (table_name.to_owned(), name.clone(), canonical_json(&index_values(index, row)),
   924	                        )
   925	                    }).collect();
   926	                for key in &keys { *self.created.entry(key.clone()).or_default() += 1; }
   927	                self.created_rows.insert(owner, keys);
   928	            }
   929	        }
   930	        #[cfg(all(feature = "sqlite", not(feature = "web-device-check")))]
   931	        if !self.event_free { partition::row_changed(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; }
   932	        #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
   933	        if !self.event_free { partition::account_row_change::<false>(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; }
   934	        #[cfg(all(feature = "sqlite", feature = "web-device-check"))]
   935	        if self.device { if !self.event_free { partition::account_row_change::<false>(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; } }
   936	        else if !self.event_free { partition::row_changed(self, table_name, old, new, origin)?; }
   937	        if origin == Origin::Source {
   938	            // @ref LLP 3000.015#3 — a source born expired never enters the count basis.
   939	            // Retire it now, in the same transaction, so a later correction/sweep
   940	            // cannot subtract a contribution which was never added. Other derived
   941	            // consumers see the same physical deletion (including an expiring update).
   942	            let new = if let Some(row) = new.filter(|row| self.expired(table, row))
   943	                && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.source == table_name && m.row_key.is_some())
   944	            {
   945	                let entries = self.tx.delete(table_name, table, row)?;
   946	                self.meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   947	                None
   948	            } else { new };
   949	            if old.is_some() || new.is_some() {
   950	                #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   951	                self.place_assets(table_name, table, old, new)?;
   952	                self.maintain(table_name, old, new)?;
   953	                if self.schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.maps(table_name)) { self.timeline_transition(table_name, old, new)?; }
   954	            }
   955	        }
   956	        self.tx.track_time_audience(
   957	            table_name,
   958	            table,
   959	            id,
   960	            new,
   961	            self.context.now.unwrap_or(i64::MIN),
   962	            if self.event_free {
   963	                new.is_some() && self.tx.time_audience_published(table_name, id)?
   964	            } else {
   965	                new.is_some_and(|row| table.live(row, self.context.now.unwrap_or(i64::MIN)))
   966	            },
   967	        )?;
   968	        Ok(())
   969	    }

   427	    /// A delete's own removal of one row, its rules already decided: receipt
   428	    /// membership, the read-through child probe, constraints, maintains and
   429	    /// the partition event. A referential cascade removes each row this way.
   430	    pub(super) fn delete_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   431	        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   432	        self.receipt_member_removed(table_name, &old)?;
   433	        self.refuse_live_children(table_name,old.field("id")?)?;
   434	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &old, Effect::Delete)?;
   435	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   436	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, &old)
   437	        })?;
   438	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), None, entries)?;

   596	    /// Stop between row removals; a short sweep can still leave due rows.
   597	    pub fn sweep_expired_for(&mut self, now: i64, limit: usize, budget: std::time::Duration) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {

   599	        // but commit physical cleanup before attempting a due opening so a
   600	        // refused publication can never wedge the rows whose upper lifetime
   601	        // has already ended.
   602	        let now = self.pin_time_audience(now)?;
   603	        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
   604	        let expiring: Vec<(String, String)> = self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().filter(|name| self.schema.tables[name].ephemeral.is_none()).filter_map(|name| {
   605	                self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index().map(|(index, _)| (name.clone(), index.to_owned()))
   606	            }).collect();
   607	        if expiring.is_empty() {
   608	            return Ok(0);
   609	        }
   610	        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
   611	        let now = time_audience::pin_writer_time(&self.schema, &tx, now)?;
   612	        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
   613	        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, Context::system().at(now), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), seq);
   614	        let mut removed = 0_u64;
   615	        let mut visited = 0_usize;
   616	        let mut expiry_after = self.expiry_after.clone();
   617	        let due = crate::store::Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   618	        let expiring = through_activation::resume_expiry_tables(
   619	            expiring.into_iter().map(|(name, _)| name).collect(), &expiry_after,
   620	        ).into_iter().map(|name| {
   621	            let index = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index().expect("expiring table").0.to_owned();
   622	            (name, index)
   623	        }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   624	        'tables: for (table_name, index) in &expiring {
   625	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   626	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(table_name).cloned();
   627	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   628	            loop {
   629	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   630	                if batch == 0 {
   631	                    break 'tables;
   632	                }
   633	                let rows = tx.scan(table_name, index, &[], &bounds, crate::store::Dir::Asc, batch)?;
   634	                let count = rows.len();
   635	                for (row, key) in rows {
   636	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   637	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(table_name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   638	                    visited += 1;
   639	                    through_activation::mark_expiry_table(&mut expiry_after, table_name);
   640	                    if removed > 0 && started.elapsed() >= budget { break 'tables; }
   641	                    match runner.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row) {
   642	                        Ok(true) => removed += 1,
   643	                        Ok(false) => {},
   644	                        // An expected reference/read-through blocker retains
   645	                        // the logically expired root. Continue by key so it
   646	                        // cannot wedge cleanup of unrelated due rows.
   647	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   648	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   649	                    }
   650	                }
   651	                if count < batch {
   652	                    expiry_after.remove(table_name);
   653	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   654	                        bounds = due.clone();
   655	                        wrapped = true;
   656	                        continue;
   657	                    }
   658	                    break;
   659	                }
   660	            }
   661	        }
   662	        let events = runner.events.take();
   663	        let tables: Vec<String> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
   664	        let written = runner.rows_written;
   665	        drop(runner);
   666	        if written > 0 {
   667	            tx.record_commit(seq, now, "expire", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, "sweep", &tables, written)?;
   668	            partition::append(&tx, seq, &events)?;
   669	        }
   670	        tx.commit()?;
   671	        self.expiry_after = expiry_after;
   672	        self.advance_time_audience(now)?;
   673	        Ok(removed)
   674	    }

   137	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
   138	    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   139	        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
   140	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   141	        let result = work(self);
   142	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
   143	        result
   144	    }

   146	    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   147	        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   148	        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
   149	        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
   150	            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
   151	            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   152	            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
   153	            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   154	            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   155	            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
   156	            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
   157	            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
   158	        }
   159	        for (key, change) in changes {
   160	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   161	            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
   162	                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
   163	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   164	                continue;
   165	            }
   166	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   167	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   168	            }
   169	        }
   170	        Ok(())
   171	    }

   173	    /// Apply a retirement's net aggregate changes, one per target row, in
   174	    /// key order. Only a total the commit really ends with can overflow.
   175	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   176	    pub(super) fn apply_retired_aggregates(&mut self, changes: BTreeMap<(String, String), (Vec<Value>, i128)>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   177	        let schema = self.schema;
   178	        for ((target, _), (key, change)) in changes {
   179	            let maintain = schema.maintain_for(&target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing maintain for {target}")))?;
   180	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   181	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   182	            }
   183	        }
   184	        Ok(())
   185	    }

   197	    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
   198	    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
   199	    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
   200	    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
   201	    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
   202	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   203	    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   204	        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
   205	        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
   206	            let target = self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].clone();
   207	            let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
   208	                let kind = target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
   209	                (field, kind)
   210	            }).collect();
   211	            let mut rows = Vec::new();
   212	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   213	            loop {
   214	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   215	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   216	                for (row, encoded) in page {
   217	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   218	                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   219	                    let key = fields.iter().map(|(field, kind)| Ok((kind.clone(), row.field(field)?.clone())))
   220	                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?;
   221	                    rows.push((old, key));
   222	                }
   223	            }
   224	            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
   225	        }
   226	
   227	        let mut ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
   228	        let mut settled = false;
   229	        for _ in 0..=legacy.len() {
   230	            let mut next_ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
   231	            for (target, rows) in &legacy {
   232	                let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
   233	                for (old, key) in rows {
   234	                    let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
   235	                        let mut value = value.clone();
   236	                        rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
   237	                        value
   238	                    }).collect();
   239	                    let next = maintained_id(&key);
   240	                    if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
   241	                }
   242	            }
   243	            if next_ids == ids {
   244	                ids = next_ids;
   245	                settled = true;
   246	                break;
   247	            }
   248	            ids = next_ids;
   249	        }
   250	        if !settled {
   251	            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()));
   252	        }
   253	
   254	        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
   255	            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
   256	                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
   257	                .collect();
   258	            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
   259	        }).collect();
   260	        let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
   261	        for (name, table, columns) in references {
   262	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   263	            loop {
   264	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   265	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   266	                for (old, encoded) in page {
   267	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   268	                    let mut next = old.clone();
   269	                    let mut changed = false;
   270	                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
   271	                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
   272	                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
   273	                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
   274	                        }
   275	                    }
   276	                    if changed {
   277	                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
   278	                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
   279	                    }
   280	                }
   281	            }
   282	        }
   283	        Ok(rewritten)
   284	    }

   286	    /// Build one aggregate from the rows in the store: the target's rows go,
   287	    /// then every source row contributes once. A schema change that adds or
   288	    /// redefines a `maintain` calls this, so a count over existing rows is
   289	    /// right from its first read (day two, LLP 2000.000 §11.2).
   290	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   291	    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   292	        let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;

   294	        self.column_rebuild |= maintain.private.is_some();
   295	        let result = self.rebuild_maintain_inner(maintain);
   296	        self.column_rebuild = saved;
   297	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
   298	        result
   299	    }

   312	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);

   314	                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
   315	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   316	                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
   317	            }
   318	        }
   319	        let source = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   320	        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(source).saturating_mul(256))?;

   325	            if page.is_empty() { break; }

   327	                self.rebuilt_source_rows += 1;

   353	        }

   356	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, Some(true))?;
   357	            }
   358	        }
   359	        Ok(())
   360	    }

     4	use super::*;
     5	
     6	pub(super) fn install(
     7	    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
     8	    schema: &Schema,
     9	    creating: bool,
    10	    generation: u64,
    11	) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    12	    let current = tx.query(
    13	        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
    14	        &[],
    15	    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
    16	    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
    17	        return Ok(generation);
    18	    }
    19	
    20	    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
    21	        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
    22	        .cloned()
    23	        .collect();
    24	    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
    25	        let mut runner = Runner::new(
    26	            tx,
    27	            schema,
    28	            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
    29	            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
    30	            tx.next_seq()?,
    31	        );
    32	        runner.event_free = true;
    33	        runner.rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&aggregates)?;
    34	        for maintain in &aggregates {
    35	            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
    36	        }
    37	    }
    38	
    39	    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
    40	        generation
    41	    } else {
    42	        generation.checked_add(1)
    43	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
    44	    };
    45	    tx.execute(
    46	        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
    47	        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
    48	    )?;
    49	    Ok(generation)
    50	}

    74	    /// Reopen the persisted compiled generation; subsequent transactions refuse
    75	    /// if another connection activates a successor.
    76	    pub fn open(mut client: Client, name: &str) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
    77	        let name = namespace(name)?;
    78	        client.batch_execute(&format!("SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
    79	        let row = client.query_one("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
    80	        if row.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
    81	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
    82	        }
    83	        let schema = decode(row.get(1))?;
    84	        let programs = decode(row.get(2))?;
    85	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
    86	        // Existing immutable stores adopt this portable admission policy at open.
    87	        // Return one offending index and its exact count, never its row payloads.
    88	        if let Some(row) = client.query(
    89	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
    90	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
    91	        )?.first() {
    92	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
    93	        }
    94	        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, None)
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.3 — read-session storage and all other upgrades
    98	    // commit together, only after every open/adoption check has succeeded.
    99	    fn attach(client: Client, mut schema: Schema, programs: BTreeMap<String, Program>, create: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   100	        let mut store = Store::new(client);
   101	        let tx = store.opening_transaction()?;
   102	        tx.batch("SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s'; SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   103	        if let Some(name) = create {
   104	            tx.batch(&format!("CREATE SCHEMA {name}; SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
   105	            tx.batch(store::DDL)?;
   106	            tx.execute("INSERT INTO _backend VALUES (true,$1,$2,$3)",
   107	                &[&store::VERSION, &canonical_json(&schema), &canonical_json(&programs)])?;
   108	        }
   109	        tx.query("SELECT seq FROM _head WHERE singleton FOR UPDATE", &[])?;
   110	        // Admission must use the backend that survived the wait for the head.
   111	        // A format change can leave schema/program bytes unchanged.
   112	        let held = tx.query("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?.remove(0);
   113	        if held.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
   114	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
   115	        }
   116	        let held_schema: Schema = decode(held.get(1))?;
   117	        let held_programs: BTreeMap<String, Program> = decode(held.get(2))?;
   118	        supported(&held_schema, &held_programs)?;
   119	        if held_schema.hash() != schema.hash() || canonical_json(&held_programs) != canonical_json(&programs) {
   120	            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend changed while opening; reopen its current generation".into()));
   121	        }
   122	        // Even a no-op ALTER takes an exclusive table lock. Reopening an
   123	        // upgraded store must remain possible while another reader holds it.
   124	        for (column, ddl) in [
   125	            ("generation", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
   126	            ("through_shortened", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN through_shortened TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"),
   127	            ("maintained_identity_version", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN maintained_identity_version TEXT"),
   128	        ] {
   129	            let exists: bool = tx.query("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = '_backend'::regclass AND attname = $1 AND NOT attisdropped)", &[&column])?[0].get(0);
   130	            if !exists { tx.batch(ddl)?; }
   131	        }
   132	        // Repeat admission under the head fence used by physical adoption.
   133	        if let Some(row) = tx.query(
   134	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
   135	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
   136	        )?.first() {
   137	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
   138	        }
   139	        tx.batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _sequences (parent TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, value BIGINT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(parent, id));")?;
   140	        tx.batch(store::READ_SESSIONS_DDL)?;
   141	        tx.batch("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq_kind;")?;
   142	        caps::install(&tx, &schema)?;
   143	        let generation = contribution_upgrade::install(&tx, &mut schema)?;
   144	        let generation = maintained_identity_upgrade::install(&tx, &schema, create.is_some(), generation)?;
   145	        // Retain the adapter's ordinary connection limits on successful open.
   146	        tx.batch("SET statement_timeout = '5s'; SET lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   147	        tx.commit()?;
   148	        store.generation = generation;
   149	        schema.prepare_delivery_lookup();
   150	        Ok(Self { store, schema, programs, ceilings: Ceilings::default(), mode: WriteMode::Serialized, retries: 0, precharge: Metered::default(), expiry_after: BTreeMap::new() })
   151	    }

     1	//! Referential actions: what deleting a referenced row does to the rows that
     2	//! name it (`on delete restrict | cascade | set null`).
     3	// @ref LLP 3000.039#2 — every reference between ordinary durable tables carries one action; restrict is the default.
     4	use super::*;

     7	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
     8	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     9	pub enum OnDelete {
    10	    Restrict,
    11	    Cascade,
    12	    SetNull,
    13	    /// The referencing row stays and names a deleted row (the pre-0.5 meaning),
    14	    /// declared on purpose: history, audit trails, contributions that outlive
    15	    /// their target.
    16	    Keep,
    17	}
    18	
    19	impl OnDelete {
    20	    pub fn words(self) -> &'static str {
    21	        match self { Self::Restrict => "on delete restrict", Self::Cascade => "on delete cascade", Self::SetNull => "on delete set null", Self::Keep => "on delete keep" }
    22	    }
    23	    /// The actions that write the children, bounded by a cap on the reference.
    24	    pub fn writes(self) -> bool { matches!(self, Self::Cascade | Self::SetNull) }
    25	    /// The actions a delete must consult (every one but `keep`).
    26	    pub fn acts(self) -> bool { self != Self::Keep }
    27	}

    29	/// One action-carrying reference `child.column -> parent`.
    30	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
    31	pub struct Referencing<'a> {
    32	    pub child: &'a str,
    33	    pub table: &'a Table,
    34	    pub column: &'a str,
    35	    pub action: OnDelete,
    36	}
    37	
    38	/// The prefix of the reference index a live child of `parent` is found under.
    39	pub const REFERENCE_INDEX_PREFIX: &str = "$reference:";

    42	/// Heap a closure keeps per reached row: its table and id (an id is at most

    48	impl Schema {
    49	    /// Whether rows of `name` take part in referential actions, as child or
    50	    /// parent: an ordinary durable application table. Ephemeral rows, engine
    51	    /// derivations and receipt/timeline bookkeeping keep their own lifetimes.
    52	    pub fn actionable(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
    53	        let Some(table) = self.table(name) else { return false };
    54	        table.ephemeral.is_none() && self.maintain_for(name).is_none() && self.private_owner(name).is_none()
    55	            && !self.is_recount_work(name) && !self.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(name))

    58	
    59	    /// Every reference into `parent` a delete consults (all but `keep`), in
    60	    /// (child, column) order.
    61	    pub fn referencing<'a>(&'a self, parent: &str) -> Vec<Referencing<'a>> {
    62	        // A plain loop into a vector: iterator adapters monomorphize per call site on the web device.
    63	        let mut out = Vec::new();
    64	        for (child, table) in &self.tables {
    65	            for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
    66	                if action.acts() && matches!(table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required), Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: target }) if target == parent) {
    67	                    out.push(Referencing { child, table, column, action: *action });
    68	                }
    69	            }
    70	        }
    71	        out
    72	    }

    74	    /// A delete of a `parent` row consults its referencing rows, so it needs
    75	    /// read authority on that row (LLP 3000.039 §3 step 1).

    78	    /// The index a reference is probed through: its column first, then the
    79	    /// child's deadline column when the child can expire, so one seek skips an
    80	    /// expired backlog. A `read through` reference uses its child index.
    81	    pub fn reference_index(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    82	        let table = self.table(child)?;
    83	        if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) {
    84	            return table.indexes.contains_key(through::CHILDREN).then_some(through::CHILDREN);
    85	        }
    86	        // The effective deadline: a read-through child's `$deadline`, else `expire at`.
    87	        let deadline = table.expiry_column();
    88	        table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| {
    89	            let columns = index.columns();
    90	            index.is_plain() && columns.first().map(String::as_str) == Some(column)
    91	                && deadline.is_none_or(|deadline| columns.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some(deadline))
    92	        }).map(|(name, _)| name.as_str())
    93	    }
    94	
    95	    /// The cap bounding a reference's children: `cap N by <column>` exactly,
    96	    /// or one when the reference itself is a plain unique key. A nullable
    97	    /// reference may have many nulls, but a parent delete probes one non-null
    98	    /// parent id, whose unique group still has at most one row.
    99	    pub fn reference_cap(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<u32> {
   100	        let table = self.table(child)?;
   101	        let declared = table.constraints.iter().find_map(|c| match c {
   102	            Constraint::Cap { by, max } if by.len() == 1 && by[0] == column => Some(*max),

   109	    /// Whether `cap` on `table` skips a group whose reference is null: only a

   115	    /// The tables a delete of a `parent` row may write through its writing
   116	    /// actions, and the tables its actions read. A function of the schema, so

   118	    pub fn action_tables(&self, parent: &str) -> ActionTables {
   119	        let mut out = ActionTables::default();
   120	        let mut queue = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   121	        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();

   146	    /// The order a delete's closure is removed in: a row before any table it

   148	    /// A cycle through those edges has no valid order and is refused.
   149	    pub fn deletion_precedes(&self, child: &str, parent: &str) -> bool {

   153	
   154	    /// A table that reaches itself through cascade and `read through` edges.
   155	    pub fn deletion_cycle(&self) -> Option<String> {
   156	        fn visit<'a>(schema: &'a Schema, name: &'a str, path: &mut Vec<&'a str>, done: &mut BTreeSet<&'a str>) -> Option<String> {
   157	            if path.contains(&name) { return Some(name.to_owned()); }
   158	            if !done.insert(name) { return None; }
   159	            path.push(name);
   160	            for (child, _) in &schema.tables {
   161	                if schema.deletion_precedes(child, name) && let Some(cycle) = visit(schema, child, path, done) { return Some(cycle); }
   162	            }
   163	            path.pop();

   169	            visit(self, name, &mut path, &mut done)

   171	    }

   173	    /// Whether `name` is a table a timeline orders the writes of.
   174	    pub fn timeline_member(&self, name: &str) -> bool {

   176	    }

   178	    /// The most rows of each table one delete of a `parent` row can reach

   181	    /// the cascade graph from `parent` is cyclic or a cascade lacks its cap.
   182	    pub fn closure_bounds(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String, u64)>> {

   184	        let mut reach: Vec<String> = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   185	        let mut edges: Vec<(usize, usize, u64)> = Vec::new();
   186	        let mut at = 0;

   197	        // Kahn's order over the reached cascade subgraph; a leftover table is a cycle.
   198	        let mut indegree = vec![0_usize; reach.len()];
   199	        for &(_, child, _) in &edges { indegree[child] += 1; }
   200	        let mut bounds = vec![0_u64; reach.len()];
   201	        bounds[0] = 1;
   202	        let mut ready: Vec<usize> = (0..reach.len()).filter(|&t| indegree[t] == 0).collect();
   203	        let mut done = 0;
   204	        while let Some(table) = ready.pop() {
   205	            done += 1;
   206	            for &(from, child, cap) in edges.iter().filter(|(from, _, _)| *from == table) {
   207	                bounds[child] = bounds[child].saturating_add(bounds[from].saturating_mul(cap));
   208	                indegree[child] -= 1;
   209	                if indegree[child] == 0 { ready.push(child); }
   210	            }
   211	        }
   212	        (done == reach.len()).then(|| reach.into_iter().zip(bounds).collect())
   213	    }
