   215	    /// The fixed charge a delete of a `parent` row reserves before it probes,
   216	    /// cascades or clears any row, over every meter: the closure's rows and
   217	    /// their identities, every restrict probe (one seek per closure row, plus
   218	    /// the closure rows it skips), every set-null row, and one engine write of
   219	    /// each, priced from the source-write plan the engine already exports. A
   220	    /// function of the schema only — caps, the reference graph, each table's
   221	    /// indexes and row size, and the exported plans — so a meter, an `E_BOUND`
   222	    /// abort or the physical allowance never depends on how many (hidden) rows
   223	    /// exist, and every host charges alike: a device's projection keeps every
   224	    /// table that can carry an action and every exported price. `None` when the
   225	    /// closure is unbounded (a cycle or a missing cap) or a written table has no
   226	    /// fixed write price. Heap is the closure's identity scratch plus the largest
   227	    /// single row's transient work, plus event images retained until commit.
   228	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — the reservation is schema-fixed; LLP 3000.015 §2's law for work shaped by hidden rows.
   229	    pub fn delete_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   230	        let bounds = self.closure_bounds(parent)?;
   231	        let mut price = [0_u64; 7];
   232	        let mut heap = 0_u64;
   233	        let mut identities = 0_u64;
   234	        let mut gathered = 0_u64;
   235	        let rows_of = |name: &str| bounds.iter().find(|(t, _)| t == name).map_or(0, |(_, n)| *n);
   236	        for (table, n) in &bounds {
   237	            let n = *n;
   238	            if table != parent {
   239	                // Fetched by the closure walk and again, current, before its delete.
   240	                let unit = self.unit_write(table)?;
   241	                heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
   242	                add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n)));
   243	                identities = identities.saturating_add(n);
   244	                // Before any set-null write, each reached cascade row proves
   245	                // that no physically retained read-through child lies outside
   246	                // the closure. Each child table can skip every reached
   247	                // identity from that table and then inspect one outside
   248	                // witness. Execution performs
   249	                // these probes under reference_prepaid, so their complete
   250	                // schema bound belongs in this outer admission reservation.
   251	                let through_children: Vec<_> = self.children(table).collect();
   252	                let probes_per_row = through_children.iter()
   253	                    .map(|(child, _, _)| rows_of(child).saturating_add(1))
   254	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   255	                let probes = n.saturating_mul(probes_per_row);
   256	                add(&mut price, [probes, 0, probes, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   257	                let outside_heap = through_children.iter()
   258	                    .map(|(name, child, _)| crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(rows_of(name).saturating_add(1)))
   259	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   260	                heap = heap.max(outside_heap);
   261	            }
   262	            for r in self.referencing(table) {
   263	                // A capped walk holds one page of child images per seek.
   264	                let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(r.table);
   265	                heap = heap.max(row.saturating_mul(REFERENCE_PAGE as u64));
   266	                let seeks = if r.table.expiry_column().is_some() && r.table.through.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| t.reference != r.column) { 2 } else { 1 };
   267	                // A walk over a capped group: a seek per page, and a last, short page per range.
   268	                let walk = |cap: u64| seeks * n + cap.saturating_mul(n) / REFERENCE_PAGE as u64;
   269	                // Every reached row runs the lifetime hook for every through
   270	                // child, including children the closure already cascaded away.
   271	                let through = r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column);
   272	                if through && table != parent { add(&mut price, [3_u64, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n))); }
   273	                match r.action {
   274	                    // A read-through child's probe: three seeks per closure row (LLP 3000.014 §6).
   275	                    OnDelete::Restrict if through => {},
   276	                    // One probe per closure row, a row per seek: it may skip the closure
   277	                    // rows that name it (each names one target per reference), then stops
   278	                    // at its first outside witness.
   279	                    OnDelete::Restrict => {
   280	                        let probe = seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n;
   281	                        add(&mut price, [2 * probe, probe, seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   282	                    }
   283	                    OnDelete::Cascade => {
   284	                        let pages = walk(u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?));
   285	                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   286	                    }
   287	                    OnDelete::SetNull => {
   288	                        let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
   289	                        gathered = gathered.max(cap);
   290	                        let cleared = cap.saturating_mul(n);
   291	                        let unit = self.unit_write(r.child)?;
   292	                        heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
   293	                        let pages = walk(cap);
   294	                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   295	                        add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(cleared)));
   296	                    }
   297	                    OnDelete::Keep => {}
   298	                }
   299	            }
   300	        }
   301	        // The root is read again, current, before its own removal.
   302	        price[2] = price[2].saturating_add(1);
   303	        // The closure's identities (table and id) are held until the last
   304	        // delete, with the root's and one page of child ids.
   305	        // A set-null group is gathered whole (at most its cap) before it is cleared.
   306	        price[4] = heap.saturating_add(identities.saturating_add(1 + REFERENCE_PAGE as u64 + gathered).saturating_mul(CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES));
   307	        let mut receiver_steps = 0;
   308	        for (table, _) in &bounds {
   309	            for reference in self.referencing(table) {
   310	                if reference.action.writes() { receiver_steps = receiver_steps.max(self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?.steps_per_write); }
   311	            }
   312	        }
   313	        price[0] = price[0].saturating_add(price[3].saturating_mul(receiver_steps));
   314	        price[4] = price[4].saturating_add(self.retained_action_heap(parent, price[3])?);
   315	        Some(price)
   316	    }

   318	    /// Diagnostic recipe price: action work plus the root's ordinary write.
   319	    /// Execution retains its existing separate charges for these two terms.
   320	    pub fn delete_total_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {

   323	        Some(total)
   324	    }

   326	    /// Event images remain live until commit, after action scratch is released.
   327	    pub fn delete_event_heap(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<u64> {
   328	        self.retained_action_heap(parent, self.delete_reservation(parent)?[3])

   106	fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
   107	    match kind {
   108	        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
   109	        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
   110	        _ => false,
   111	    }
   112	}
   113	
   114	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   115	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   116	    match rule {
   117	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   118	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   119	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   120	        _ => false,
   121	    }
   122	}
   123	
   124	fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   125	    match rule {
   126	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   127	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   128	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   129	        _ => false,
   130	    }
   131	}

   133	impl Schema {
   134	    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
   135	    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
   136	        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
   137	            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
   138	    }
   139	    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
   140	        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
   141	    }
   142	}

   144	impl Serialize for Schema {
   145	    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
   146	        let required = self.required_capabilities();
   147	        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
   148	        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
   149	        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
   150	        let mut wire = self.clone();
   151	        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
   152	            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
   153	        }
   154	        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
   155	            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
   156	        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
   157	        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
   158	    }
   159	}

   161	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {

   164	        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.

   173	                    carriers += 1;

   176	                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
   177	                    recorded += 1;
   178	                    false
   179	                } else { true }

   182	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));

   184	            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
   185	        }

   187	            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {

   189	            }
   190	        }

   192	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
   193	        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
   194	        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
   195	        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
   196	        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
   197	            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");

   199	        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
   200	        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
   201	            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
   202	            else { required.remove(cap); }

+    // Maintained-view evaluation is outside the Lean oracle. Exercise its
+    // physical identity as an explicit generator invariant, so these cases
+    // cannot be counted as oracle passes merely because they are unsupported.
+    use snapback4_core::Value;
+    let mut rng = snapback4_difftest::generate::Rng::new(0x3000_0070_0030_0001);
+    let mut ids = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
+    for n in 0..256 {
+        let key = if n == 0 {
+            vec![]
+        } else {
+            let principal = format!("p{:063}", rng.next());
+            let reference = format!("r{:063}", rng.next());
+            let len = rng.pick(65) as usize;
+            let token = format!("{:016x}", rng.next()).repeat(4)[..len].to_owned();
+            vec![Value::Id(principal), Value::Id(reference), Value::String(token),
+                 Value::Int((rng.next() & ((1 << 53) - 1)) as i64)]
+        };
+        let id = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        assert_eq!(id.len(), 64, "seeded case {n}: {key:?}");
+        assert!(id.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit() && !byte.is_ascii_uppercase()));
+        assert!(snapback4_core::value::identity_fits(&id));
+        assert_eq!(id, snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key));
+        assert!(ids.insert(id), "unexpected digest collision in generated corpus");
+    }
+}

--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+import Quarry.Store
+
+/-!
+# Maintained aggregate identity
+
+The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
+tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
+cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
+store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
+lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
+and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
+identity while publishing the new version.
+-/
+
+namespace Quarry
+
+/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
+migration. -/
+def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
+
+/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
+not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
+to this logical model. -/
+def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
+  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
+    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
+    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
+
+theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
+  simp [maintainedIdV1]
+
+/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
+byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
+theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
+  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
+  omega
+
+def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
+  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
+
+structure MaintainedState where
+  version : Nat
+  rows : List Row
+
+/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
+identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
+states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
+def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
+    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
+  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
+example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
+  maintainedIdV1_length _
+
+end Quarry

    41	    pub(super) fn capture_insert(&mut self, name: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<Supplied, RuntimeError> {
    42	        let result = self.capture_insert_inner(name, row);
    43	        self.trace_authorization(&result, name, Effect::Insert, "read through capture");
    44	        result
    45	    }

    47	    fn capture_insert_inner(
    48	        &mut self,
    49	        name: &str,
    50	        row: Supplied,
    51	    ) -> Result<Supplied, RuntimeError> {
    52	        let table = &self.schema.tables[name];
    53	        let Some(through) = &table.through else {
    54	            return Ok(row);
    55	        };
    56	        let mut row = row.into_value();
    57	        let id = row
    58	            .field(&through.reference)
    59	            .ok()
    60	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
    61	            .ok_or_else(|| self.rule_refusal(name, Effect::Insert, "read through parent reference"))?;
    62	        let parent = &self.schema.tables[&through.parent];
    63	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — the parent lookup is authorization work under the
    64	        // request's physical allowance; reserve_capture prepaid its logical charges.
    65	        let found = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.get(scope, &through.parent, id))?.filter(|r| !self.expired(parent, r));
    66	        if self.device {
    67	            let covered = if let Some(found) = &found {
    68	                self.is_provisional(&through.parent, found)? || self.device_work(|runner| {
    69	                    let viewer = runner.context.viewer.clone();
    70	                    let now = runner.context.now.unwrap_or(0);
    71	                    runner.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.recording_covered(&through.parent, found, &viewer, now, scope, &mut runner.meter))
    72	                })?
    73	            } else { false };
    74	            if !covered { return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("read through .{} needs a live, covered {} parent; queued without a row", through.reference, through.parent))); }
    75	        }
    76	        let found = found.ok_or_else(|| self.rule_refusal(name, Effect::Insert, "read through parent missing or expired"))?;
    77	        stamp(parent, through, &found, &mut row)?;
    78	        table.recompute_deadline(&mut row)?;
    79	        if !self.context.is_system() {
    80	            let viewer = self.context.viewer.clone();
    81	            let readable = self.authorized_scratch(self.rule_scratch(&table.rules.read), &[], |runner, allowance| {
    82	                rules::evaluate(&table.rules.read, &viewer, None, &row, false, &mut super::read::PrefixProbe { runner, allowance })
    83	            })?;
    84	            if !readable {
    85	                // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#5 — only the developer trace names the unread parent.
    86	                self.refusing_phase(&through.parent, &format!("insert into {name} needs unread parent {} through .{}", through.parent, through.reference), "read rule");
    87	                return Err(RuntimeError::Rule { table: name.into(), effect: Effect::Insert });
    88	            }
    89	        }
    90	        Ok(row.capture_input(&CaptureInput(())))
    91	    }

    93	    pub(super) fn physical_children(
    94	        &mut self,
    95	        parent: &str,
    96	        id: &Value,
    97	    ) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    98	        self.physical_children_outside(parent, id, &BTreeSet::new())
    99	    }
   100	
   101	    /// Whether a read-through child remains outside a delete's cascade
   102	    /// closure. Children in `deleting` are removed first by deletion_order and
   103	    /// therefore do not physically retain their parent.
   104	    pub(super) fn physical_children_outside(
   105	        &mut self,
   106	        parent: &str,
   107	        id: &Value,
   108	        deleting: &BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
   109	    ) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   110	        let children: Vec<_> = self
   111	            .schema
   112	            .children(parent)
   113	            .map(|(n, _, _)| {
   114	                // Only identities from this child table can appear in its
   115	                // index scan. Identities from other closure tables cannot
   116	                // consume a row in this table's prefix.
   117	                let inside = deleting.iter().filter(|(table, _)| table == n).count();
   118	                (n.clone(), inside.saturating_add(1))
   119	            })
   120	            .collect();
   121	        // Reserve the complete schema-fixed probe set before its first seek.
   122	        // Never short-circuit on an occupied table, including at low ceilings.
   123	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — the seeks draw from the request's physical allowance; occupancy never selects the logical charge.
   124	        let heap = children.iter().map(|(name, limit)| super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[name]).saturating_mul(*limit as u64)).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   125	        let probes = children.iter().map(|(_, limit)| *limit as u64).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   126	        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, probes), (MeterKind::Steps, probes), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap)], |runner, scope| {
   127	            let mut occupied = false;
   128	            for (name, limit) in &children {
   129	                let rows = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, *limit)?;
   130	                occupied |= rows.into_iter().any(|(row, _)| row.field("id").ok().and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
   131	                    .is_none_or(|child| !deleting.contains(&(name.clone(), child.to_owned()))));
   132	            }
   133	            Ok(occupied)
   134	        })
   135	    }
   136	
   137	    // A deadline suffix skips an arbitrary expired backlog in one seek.
   138	    pub(super) fn refuse_live_children(
   139	        &mut self,
   140	        parent: &str,
   141	        id: &Value,
   142	    ) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   143	        let children: Vec<_> = self
   144	            .schema
   145	            .children(parent)
   146	            .map(|(n, _, _)| n.clone())
   147	            .collect();
   148	        if children.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }
   149	        let now = self
   150	            .context
   151	            .now
   152	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("delete clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   153	        let heap = children
   154	            .iter()
   155	            .map(|n| super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[n]).saturating_mul(3))
   156	            .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   157	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — three schema-fixed seeks per child table, each drawn from the request's physical allowance.
   158	        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, children.len() as u64 * 3), (MeterKind::Steps, children.len() as u64 * 3), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap)], |runner, scope| {
   159	            if runner.device {
   160	                let occupied = runner.device_work(|runner| runner.current_children(parent, id, &children))?;
   161	                return if occupied { Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent)) } else { Ok(()) };
   162	            }
   163	            for name in &children {
   164	                let never = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone(), Value::Null], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 1)?;
   165	                let finite = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds { gt: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() }, Dir::Asc, 1)?;
   166	                if !never.is_empty() || !finite.is_empty() {
   167	                    return Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent));
   168	                }
   169	                // §3.3 forbids physical removal even when §6's live probe is empty.
   170	                // The author's implementation ruling keeps this case fail-closed.
   171	                if !runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 1)?.is_empty() {
   172	                    return Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent));
   173	                }
   174	            }
   175	            Ok(())
   176	        })
   177	    }
   178	
   179	    pub(super) fn parent_has_children(&self, parent: &str) -> RuntimeError {
   180	        RuntimeError::Structural {
   181	            code: "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN",
   182	            message: format!("{parent} at {} has stored children; delete its live read-through children and sweep expired children, then retry `delete {parent}[id]` (guide rules)", self.statement_site),
   183	        }
   184	    }
   185	
   186	    // @ref LLP 3000.014#5 — retained history cannot terminally refuse a
   187	    // current delete. Mismatched, expired or uncovered witnesses must queue.
   188	    fn current_children(&mut self, parent: &str, id: &Value, children: &[String]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   189	        if children.is_empty() { return Ok(false); }
   190	        let uncertain = || RuntimeError::Prediction("parent deletion needs complete matching current child coverage; queued without a row".into());
   191	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   192	        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[parent]))?;
   193	        // Device-only work over held state: the token counts it on the device's separate physical allowance.
   194	        let parent_id = id.as_str()?.to_owned();
   195	        let parent_row = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.get(scope, parent, &parent_id))?.ok_or_else(uncertain)?;
   196	        for name in children {
   197	            let table = &self.schema.tables[name];
   198	            let through = table.through.as_ref().unwrap();
   199	            if !self.child_coverage(name, through, &parent_row)? { return Err(uncertain()); }
   200	            let table_scratch = self.meter.mark();
   201	            // Expected captures plus a reusable row/cursor, reserved before seeking.
   202	            self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(table).saturating_mul(3))?;
   203	            let mut expected = crate::value::object([] as [(&str, Value); 0]);
   204	            stamp(&self.schema.tables[parent], through, &parent_row, &mut expected)?;
   205	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   206	            loop {
   207	                let scratch = self.meter.mark();
   208	                self.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   209	                self.meter.step(through.fields.len() as u64 + 1)?;
   210	                let page = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.scan_metered(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 1, &mut runner.meter))?;

@@ -148,7 +148,15 @@ rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
 rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
 advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
 the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
-writer/head fence. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
+legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
+then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps. Thus an
+aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
+aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
+to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
+target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
+Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
+the same transaction. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
 `maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
 it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
 zero.

 `restrict`, a read-through child, the meter) aborts the whole mutation, and
 nothing commits.
 
+An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
+logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
+store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
+`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its
+image yet.
+
 **Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
 is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
 can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
@@ -271,6 +277,14 @@ bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
 not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
 constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
 
+For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
+authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine
+then retires the predecessor through the action path before the remaining
+uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
+or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
+refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
+earlier cascade and set-null writes.
+
 A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
 the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically

   465	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   466	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   467	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   468	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   469	            ));
   470	        }
   471	        let now = self
   472	            .context
   473	            .now
   474	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   475	        let mut count = 0;
   476	        let mut visited = 0;
   477	        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
   478	        for name in tables {
   479	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   480	                continue;
   481	            };
   482	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   483	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   484	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   485	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   486	            while visited < limit {
   487	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   488	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   489	                    runner
   490	                        .tx
   491	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   492	                })?;
   493	                if page.is_empty() {
   494	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   495	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   496	                        bounds = due.clone();
   497	                        wrapped = true;
   498	                        continue;
   499	                    }
   500	                    break;
   501	                }
   502	                let page_len = page.len();
   503	                for (row, key) in page {
   504	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   505	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   506	                    visited += 1;
   507	                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
   508	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   509	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   510	                        Ok(false) => {},
   511	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   512	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   513	                    }
   514	                }
   515	                if page_len < batch {
   516	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   517	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   518	                        bounds = due.clone();
   519	                        wrapped = true;
   520	                        continue;
   521	                    }
   522	                    break;
   523	                }
   524	            }
   525	        }
   526	        Ok(count)
   527	    }
   528	}

table conversations:
  title: text <=100
  read <- allow
  insert <- allow
  sync public
table members:
  conversationId: conversations
  principal: principal
  readUpTo: int default 0
  joinedAt: int default 0
  unique conversationId, principal
  cap 100 by conversationId
  read <- allow
  insert <- allow
  update <- allow
  delete <- allow
  sync public
table messages:
  conversationId: conversations
  ordinal: int
  senderId: principal
  tombstone: bool default false
  until: time ?
  expire at .until
  read <- allow
  insert <- allow
  update <- allow
  delete <- allow
  sync public
view unread: count messages by members m
  where .conversationId = m.conversationId and .ordinal > m.readUpTo
    and .senderId != m.principal and not .tombstone and .ordinal > m.joinedAt
query unreadFor(member: members):
  return unread[member]
query unreadRows():
  return unread first 100
mutation join(id: id, conversationId: conversations, principal: principal, readUpTo: int, joinedAt: int):
  insert members { id, conversationId, principal, readUpTo, joinedAt }
mutation send(id: id, conversationId: conversations, ordinal: int, senderId: principal, until: time ?):
  insert messages { id, conversationId, ordinal, senderId, until }
mutation mark(member: members, readUpTo: int):
  update members[member] { readUpTo }
mutation tombstone(message: messages):
  update messages[message] { tombstone: true }
mutation edit(message: messages, ordinal: int, senderId: principal):
  update messages[message] { ordinal, senderId }
mutation remove(message: messages):
  delete messages[message]
mutation leave(member: members):
  delete members[member]
//! Lifetime topology is generated independently of the source's lifetime.
use super::*;
use crate::{ir::Program, partition};
#[path = "field_tests.rs"] mod fields;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
enum Lifetime { Direct, Inherited, Through }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
struct Config { lifetime: Lifetime, source_expiry: bool, member_expiry: bool, default_mark: i64, tombstones: bool }
fn backend(c: Config) -> (Schema, Vec<Program>) {
    let member_life = match c.lifetime {
        Lifetime::Direct => "read <- exists access[.conversationId, viewer]",
        Lifetime::Inherited => "read through .conversationId\n  immutable conversationId",
        Lifetime::Through => "lease: leases\n  immutable lease\n  read through .lease",
    };
    let text = format!(r#"
table conversations:
  until: time ?
  {parent_expiry}
  immutable until
  public
  sync public
table access:
  conversationId: conversations
  principal: principal
  unique conversationId, principal
  public
  sync public
table leases:
  room: conversations
  immutable room
  read through .room
  insert <- allow
  sync
table members:
  conversationId: conversations
  principal: principal
  mark: int default {mark}
  until: time ?
  cap 100 by conversationId
  {member_life}
  {member_expiry}
  insert <- allow
  update <- allow
  delete <- allow
  sync
table messages:
  conversationId: conversations
  ordinal: int
  senderId: principal
  tombstone: bool default false
  until: time ?
  {expiry}
  insert <- allow
  update <- allow
  delete <- allow
  public
  sync public
view unread: count messages by members m
  where .conversationId = m.conversationId and .ordinal > m.mark
    and .senderId != m.principal {predicate}
query pair(member: members, room: conversations):
  return {{ value: unread[member], sources: messages where .conversationId = room first 100 }}
mutation remove(message: messages):
  delete messages[message]
mutation extend(member: members, until: time):
  update members[member] {{ until }}
"#, mark=c.default_mark,
        parent_expiry=if c.member_expiry {"expire at .until"} else {""},
        member_expiry=if c.member_expiry && !matches!(c.lifetime,Lifetime::Inherited) {"expire at .until"} else {""},
        expiry=if c.source_expiry { "expire at .until" } else { "" },
        predicate=if c.tombstones { "and not .tombstone" } else { "" });
    let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("lifetimes.q".into(), text)]);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    (crate::json_codec::from_text(&crate::json_codec::to_text(&b.schema).unwrap()).unwrap(),
     crate::json_codec::from_text(&crate::json_codec::to_text(&b.programs.into_iter().map(|p|p.program).collect::<Vec<_>>()).unwrap()).unwrap())
}
fn put_field(row: Value, key: &str, value: Value) -> Value {
    let mut fields = row.as_object().unwrap().clone(); fields.insert(key.into(), value); Value::Row(fields.into())
}
fn recipient(c: Config, n: usize, group: usize, until: Option<i64>, mark: Option<i64>) -> Value {
    let mut row = object([("id", id(&format!("u{n}"))), ("conversationId", id(&format!("r{group}"))),
        ("principal", id(&format!("p{n}"))), ("until", until.map(Value::Int).unwrap_or(Value::Null))]);
    if let Some(mark) = mark { row = put_field(row, "mark", Value::Int(mark)); }
    if matches!(c.lifetime, Lifetime::Through) { row = put_field(row, "lease", id(&format!("l{group}"))); }
    row
}
fn source(n: usize, group: usize, ordinal: i64, until: Option<i64>) -> Value {
    put_field(message(n, ordinal, 99, false, until), "conversationId", id(&format!("r{group}")))
}
fn seed_parents(e: &mut Engine) {
    e.seed_at((0..2).flat_map(|n| [
        ("conversations".into(), object([("id", id(&format!("r{n}"))), ("until", Value::Int(2000 + n * 2000))])),
        ("leases".into(), object([("id", id(&format!("l{n}"))), ("room", id(&format!("r{n}")))])),
        ("access".into(), object([("id", id(&format!("a{n}"))), ("conversationId", id(&format!("r{n}"))), ("principal", id("reader"))]))]), 1).unwrap();
}
fn config(lifetime: Lifetime) -> Config { Config { lifetime, source_expiry: false, member_expiry: true, default_mark: 0, tombstones: true } }

// Independent raw fact model: no engine expiry selector, row-key predicate,
// evidence, stored count or scalar/acquisition dispatch decides these answers.
fn member_live(c: Config, u: &Value, now: i64) -> bool {
    if !c.member_expiry { return true; }
    let group = u.field("conversationId").unwrap().as_str().unwrap();
    match c.lifetime {
        Lifetime::Direct => live(u, now),
        Lifetime::Inherited => now < if group == "r0" { 2000 } else { 4000 },
        Lifetime::Through => live(u, now) && now < if u.field("lease").unwrap() == &id("l0") { 2000 } else { 4000 },
    }
}
fn expected(c: Config, u: &Value, messages: &BTreeMap<usize, Value>, now: i64) -> Option<i64> {
    member_live(c, u, now).then(|| messages.values().filter(|m|
        (!c.source_expiry || live(m, now))
        && m.field("conversationId").unwrap() == u.field("conversationId").unwrap()
        && field(m, "ordinal") > u.field("mark").ok().and_then(|v|v.as_int().ok()).unwrap_or(c.default_mark)
        && m.field("senderId").unwrap() != u.field("principal").unwrap()
        && (!c.tombstones || m.field("tombstone").unwrap() == &Value::Bool(false))).count() as i64)
}
fn check_rows(tx: &crate::store::Tx<'_>, schema: &Schema, c: Config, members: &BTreeMap<usize, Value>, messages: &BTreeMap<usize, Value>, now: i64, label: &str) -> usize {
    let views: Vec<_> = tx.scan("unread", "byId", &[], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 256).unwrap().into_iter().map(|(v,_)|v).collect();
    assert_eq!(views.len(), members.len(), "{label} materialized member count");
    let runner = || Runner::new(tx, schema, Context::new("reader", Default::default()).at(now), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Cap), 0);
    let mut stream = runner(); let mut cold = runner(); let mut scalar = runner();
    let batches = stream.live_aggregate_batch("unread", &views).unwrap();
    let acquisition = cold.live_acquisition_batch("unread", &views).unwrap();
    let mut comparisons = 0;
    for ((view, batch), acquired) in views.iter().zip(batches).zip(acquisition) {
        let name = view.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap();
        let n: usize = name[1..].parse().unwrap();
        let want = expected(c, &members[&n], messages, now);
        comparisons += fields::predicates(tx, schema, c, &members[&n], want, now, label);
        // Every path compares separately with facts, so two dispatches agreeing
        // on the same stale cache cannot satisfy the acquisition comparison.
        for (path, image) in [("scalar", scalar.live_aggregate("unread", view.clone()).unwrap()), ("batch", batch), ("acquisition", acquired)] {
            assert_eq!(image.as_ref().map(|v|field(v,"value")), want, "{label} {path} member={name} clock={now} config={c:?}");
            if let Some(image) = image { assert!(!pending(&image), "{label} {path} incomplete"); }
            comparisons += 1;
        }
    }
    // The actual transport entry points must also cross the dispatch guard.
    let snapshot = partition::snapshot_page(tx, schema, "reader", None, 10000, now).unwrap();
    assert!(snapshot.next.is_none());
    let stream = partition::stream(tx, schema, "reader", 0, 10000, now).unwrap();
    assert!(!stream.more);
    let snapshot: Vec<_> = snapshot.events.into_iter().filter(|e| e.table == "unread" && e.kind == partition::EventKind::Put).map(|e|(e.id,e.data)).collect();
    let stream: Vec<_> = stream.events.into_iter().filter(|e| e.table == "unread" && e.kind == "put").map(|e|(e.id,e.data)).collect();
    for (path, events) in [("snapshot", snapshot), ("stream", stream)] {
        let mut delivered = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        for (id, data) in events {
            let n: usize = id[1..].parse().unwrap();
            let want = members.get(&n).and_then(|u|expected(c,u,messages,now));
            assert_eq!(data.as_ref().map(|v|field(v,"value")), want, "{label} transport {path} id={n}");
            assert!(!pending(data.as_ref().unwrap()));
            delivered.insert(n); comparisons += 1;
        }
        for (&n, u) in members { if expected(c,u,messages,now).is_some() { assert!(delivered.contains(&n), "{label} {path} omitted u{n}"); } }
    }
    comparisons
}

fn reproduction(lifetime: Lifetime) {
    let c = config(lifetime); let (schema, programs) = backend(c);
    let mut e = Engine::memory(schema, programs).unwrap(); seed_parents(&mut e);
    let insertion = matches!(lifetime, Lifetime::Direct);
    let u = recipient(c, 0, 0, Some(10), Some(0));
    let m = source(0, 0, 1, None);
    e.seed_at([("members".into(), u.clone())], if insertion {1} else {1000}).unwrap();
    e.seed_at([("messages".into(), m.clone())], if insertion {11} else {1000}).unwrap();
    if !insertion {
        e.mutate("lifetimes.remove", None, Context::new("reader", BTreeMap::from([("message".into(),id("m0"))])).at(2500)).unwrap();
    }
    let now = if insertion {9} else {1500};
    let result = e.query("lifetimes.pair", Context::new("reader", BTreeMap::from([("member".into(),id("u0")),("room".into(),id("r0"))])).at(now)).unwrap();
    let want = i64::from(insertion);
    assert!(result.complete);
    let sources = result.data.field("sources").unwrap().as_array().unwrap().len() as i64;
    eprintln!("BG round3 literal {lifetime:?}: value={:?} authorized_sources={sources} complete={}", result.data.field("value"), result.complete);
    assert_eq!(result.data.field("value"), Ok(&Value::Int(sources)), "literal {lifetime:?} same-query authorized sources");
    assert_eq!(sources, want);
    let schema = e.schema().clone(); let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
    check_rows(&tx,&schema,c,&BTreeMap::from([(0,u)]),&if insertion {BTreeMap::from([(0,m)])} else {BTreeMap::new()},now,"literal");
}
#[test] fn nonexpiring_source_direct_member_rollback() { reproduction(Lifetime::Direct); }
#[test] fn nonexpiring_source_inherited_member_rollback() { reproduction(Lifetime::Inherited); }

    60	        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    61	    } else {
    62	        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    63	    };
    64	    let mut limit=32i64;
    65	    let page_mark=meter.mark();
    66	    loop {
    67	        limit=work.limit(meter,limit as usize) as i64;
    68	        let size=tx.query(sizes,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
    69	        let bytes=size[0].get::<_,i64>(0) as u64;
    70	        let count=size[0].get::<_,i64>(1) as u64;
    71	        // Network/read buffers, retained driver rows and their metadata. Typed
    72	        // JSON decode is priced from borrowed text later, one row at a time;
    73	        // the query scan's conservative 256x all-rows decoder is inappropriate
    74	        // for this walk. This initial estimate is followed by a scratch check
    75	        // before any adoption callback runs.
    76	        let reservation=bytes.saturating_mul(8).saturating_add(count.saturating_mul(1024));
    77	        if limit>1 && reservation>meter.ceilings.heap_bytes/2 { limit/=2; continue; }
    78	        meter.heap(reservation)?;
    79	        let query=if after.is_some() {
    80	            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
    81	        } else {
    82	            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
    83	        };
    84	        let page=tx.query(query,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
    85	        if adoption::page_fits(page.iter().map(|raw| raw.get::<_,&str>(1)), meter, work,
    86	            Some(&|row| adoption::contribution_bytes(row,schema)))? { return Ok(page); }
    87	        limit=(page.len() as i64/2).max(1);
    88	        drop(page);
    89	        meter.release_heap(page_mark.clone());
    90	    }
    91	}
     1	//! The same capture barrier, restore validation and child-first sweep on Postgres.
     2	// @ref LLP 3000.014#7-activation — publish captures, indexes and generation in one transaction.
     3	use super::*;
     4	
     5	impl PostgresEngine {
     6	    pub fn read_through_shortened(&mut self) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, u64>, RuntimeError> {
     7	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
     8	        let counts = decode(
     9	            tx.query(
    10	                "SELECT through_shortened FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
    11	                &[],
    12	            )?[0]
    13	                .get(0),
    14	        )?;
    15	        tx.rollback()?;
    16	        Ok(counts)
    17	    }
    18	    pub fn sweep_expired(&mut self, now: i64, limit: usize) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    19	        let tx = self.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized))?;
    20	        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
    21	        let mut runner = Runner::new(
    22	            &tx,
    23	            &self.schema,
    24	            Context::system().at(now),
    25	            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
    26	            seq,
    27	        );
    28	        let mut expiry_after = self.expiry_after.clone();
    29	        let count = runner.sweep_server_rows(limit, &mut expiry_after)?;
    30	        let events = runner.events.take();
    31	        let tables: Vec<_> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
    32	        let writes = runner.rows_written;
    33	        drop(runner);
    34	        if writes > 0 {
    35	            tx.record_commit(
    36	                seq,
    37	                now,
    38	                "expire",
    39	                crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL,
    40	                "sweep",
    41	                &tables,
    42	                writes,
    43	            )?;
    44	            partition::append(&tx, seq, &events)?;
    45	        }
    46	        tx.commit()?;
    47	        self.expiry_after = expiry_after;
    48	        Ok(count)
    49	    }
    50	
    51	    pub fn load_trusted(
    52	        &mut self,
    53	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    54	        now: i64,
    55	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    56	        let tx = self.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized))?;
    57	        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
    58	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
    59	        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
    60	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
    61	        let mut count = 0;
    62	        let mut runner = Runner::new(
    63	            &tx,
    64	            &self.schema,
    65	            Context::system().at(now),
    66	            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
    67	            seq,
    68	        );
    69	        for (name, mut row) in rows {
    70	            let table = self
    71	                .schema
    72	                .table(&name)
    73	                .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {name}")))?;
    74	            table.recompute_deadline(&mut row)?;
    75	            validate::validate_row(&self.schema, &name, &row)?;
    76	            let old = tx.get(&name, row.field("id")?.as_str()?)?;
    77	            tx.put(&name, table, &row, old.as_ref())?;
    78	            partition::row_changed(
    79	                &mut runner,
    80	                &name,
    81	                old.as_ref(),
    82	                Some(&row),
    83	                crate::engine::write::Origin::Source,
    84	            )?;
    85	            runner.written_tables.insert(name);
    86	            count += 1;
    87	        }
    88	        super::super::through_activation::validate_restore(&tx, &self.schema, now)?;
    89	        let events = runner.events.take();
    90	        let tables: Vec<_> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
    91	        drop(runner);
    92	        if count > 0 {
    93	            tx.record_commit(
    94	                seq,
    95	                now,
    96	                "restore",
    97	                crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL,
    98	                "restore",
    99	                &tables,
   100	                count,
   101	            )?;
   102	            partition::append(&tx, seq, &events)?;
   103	        }
   104	        tx.commit()?;
   105	        Ok(count)
   106	    }
   107	
   108	    pub fn adopt_at(
   109	        &mut self,
   110	        mut schema: Schema,
   111	        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
   112	        now: i64,
   113	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   114	        schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
   115	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#5 — adoption replaces tracked membership and any shared binding index.
   116	        schema.prepare_delivery_lookup();
   117	        let programs: BTreeMap<_, _> = programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)).collect();
   118	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
   119	        let generation = self
   120	            .generation()
   121	            .checked_add(1)
   122	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?;
   123	        let tx = self.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized))?;
   124	        let shortened =
   125	            super::super::through_activation::activate(&tx, &schema, Some(&self.schema), now)?;
   126	        tx.execute("DELETE FROM i", &[])?;
   127	        tx.execute("DELETE FROM _cap_counts", &[])?;
   128	        for name in self
   129	            .schema
   130	            .tables
   131	            .keys()
   132	            .filter(|n| !schema.tables.contains_key(*n))
   133	        {
   134	            tx.execute("DELETE FROM r WHERE t=$1", &[name])?;
   135	        }
   136	        for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
   137	            let mut after = String::new();
   138	            loop {
   139	                let page = tx.query(
   140	                    "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT 256",
   141	                    &[name, &after],
   142	                )?;
   143	                if page.is_empty() {
   144	                    break;
   145	                }
   146	                for item in page {
   147	                    after = item.get(0);
   148	                    let mut row: Value = decode(item.get(1))?;
   149	                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
   150	                        fields.retain(|f, _| table.columns.contains_key(f));
   151	                    }
   152	                    table.recompute_deadline(&mut row)?;
   153	                    validate::validate_row(&schema, name, &crate::schema::row_image(&row, table))?;
   154	                    tx.execute("DELETE FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id=$2", &[name, &after])?;
   155	                    tx.put(name, table, &row, None)?;
   156	                }
   157	            }
   158	        }
   159	        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
   160	        let mut runner = Runner::new(
   161	            &tx,
   162	            &schema,
   163	            Context::system().at(now),
   164	            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
   165	            seq,
   166	        );
   167	        runner.event_free = true;
   168	        for m in schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m| m.private.is_none()) {
   169	            runner.rebuild_maintain(m)?;
   170	        }
   171	        let parents = super::super::column_activation::changed_parents(&schema, Some(&self.schema));
   172	        runner.activate_columns(
   173	            Some(&self.schema),
   174	            &schema.maintains.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
   175	            &parents,
   176	            None,
   177	        )?;
   178	        drop(runner);
   179	        super::super::through_activation::validate_indexes(&tx, &schema)?;
   180	        tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET schema=$1, programs=$2, generation=$3, through_shortened=$4, maintained_identity_version=$5 WHERE singleton",&[
   181	            &canonical_json(&schema), &canonical_json(&programs), &(generation as i64),
   182	            &canonical_json(&shortened), &crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION,
   183	        ])?;
   184	        tx.commit()?;
   185	        self.schema = schema;
   186	        self.programs = programs;
   187	        self.store.generation = generation;
   188	        self.expiry_after.clear();
   189	        Ok(generation)
   190	    }
   191	}

   130	Spellings are illustrative. None of the blocks below is a compiling example.
   131	
   132	### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
   133	
   134	Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
   135	64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
   136	`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
   137	The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
   138	identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
   139	adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
   140	address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
   141	
   142	The intrinsic `byId` order of aggregate rows is consequently opaque digest
   143	order. It is stable for one identity version but has no relationship to the
   144	lexical or numeric order of group fields, and migration may change it. A query
   145	whose result needs group-key order declares that order explicitly (for example,
   146	`first 50 by .emoji`) rather than relying on an unqualified aggregate scan.
   147	
   148	The SQLite metadata and evaluation-PostgreSQL backend marker
   149	`maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` bind persisted aggregate targets to that
   150	function. Opening or adopting either store without the marker — including a
   151	0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON of the group key —
   152	atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate target from its source
   153	rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
   154	rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
   155	advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
   156	the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
   157	writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
   158	legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
   159	then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps. Thus an
   160	aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
   161	aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
   162	to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
   163	target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
   164	Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
   165	the same transaction. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
   166	`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
   167	it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
   168	zero.
   169	
   170	### 3.1 F1: maintained columns
   171	
   172	F1 is LLP 3000.007.001, unchanged. Its value here is ranking. With `likeCount`
   173	on the post and ruling 29's hour index, Trending becomes one merge over 25 hour
   174	lanes (§21.3 P3):
   175	
   176	- zero-like posts are included;
   177	- ties break by post time;
   178	- there is no copied time and no fill.
   179

     1	import Quarry.Eval
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Writes: rule checks and refusals
     5	
     6	From the rules card, `why E_RULE`, `why NOT_FOUND`, `why E_CONFLICT` and the
     7	writes card:
     8	
     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on
    10	  `id` or a declared unique key with a hidden row is `E_RULE`; with a visible
    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
    12	  or the key's `else CODE`.
    13	* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
    16	  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
    18	  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
    19	  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is
    20	  the row if it is readable afterwards, else null.
    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
    22	  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.
    23	* **delete** — `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or unreadable refused target,
    24	  `E_RULE` for a readable one whose delete rule refuses. A row that
    25	  `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` references name also needs read
    26	  authority (`NOT_FOUND`); then its delete closes over `cascade` references,
    27	  refuses `E_REFERENCED` while a `restrict` reference names a closure row
    28	  from outside the closure, clears `set null` references outside it, and
    29	  removes the closure (LLP 3000.039 §3).
    30	
    31	The order in which checks run when several fail is not documented; the
    32	model's order is OPEN W1–W6.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	namespace Quarry
    36	
    37	def notFound : Stop := .refuse "NOT_FOUND"
    38	def eRule : Stop := .refuse "E_RULE"
    39	def eInput : Stop := .refuse "E_INPUT"
    40	
    41	def toScalarE : Value → Except Stop Scalar
    42	  | .s x => pure x
    43	  | _ => throw eInput
    44	
    45	def scalarsE (fs : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    46	  fs.mapM fun p => do return (p.1, ← toScalarE p.2)
    47	
    48	/-- A column value fits its declaration: only a nullable column takes null. -/
    49	def fits (c : ColDecl) (x : Scalar) : Bool := c.nullable || x != .null
    50	
    51	/-- The new image of an insert. An absent nullable column is null; an absent
    52	required column refuses with `missing`. Unknown fields refuse `E_INPUT`. -/
    53	def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))
    54	    (missing : Stop) : Except Stop Row := do
    55	  if fields.any fun p => p.1 != "id" && !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
    56	  let cols ← td.cols.mapM fun c => match fields.lookup c.name with
    57	    | some x => if fits c x then pure (c.name, x) else throw eInput
    58	    | none => if c.nullable then pure (c.name, Scalar.null) else throw missing
    59	  return { id := rid, cols }
    60	
    61	/-- The next image of an update: the patch replaces named columns. -/
    62	def patchImage (td : TableDecl) (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop Row := do
    63	  if patch.any fun p => !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
    64	  let cols ← old.cols.mapM fun p => match patch.lookup p.1 with
    65	    | some x =>
    66	      match td.cols.find? (·.name == p.1) with
    67	      | some c => if fits c x then pure (p.1, x) else throw eInput
    68	      | none => throw eInput
    69	    | none => pure p
    70	  return { old with cols }
    71	
    72	def keyOf (cols : List String) (r : Row) : List (String × Scalar) := cols.map fun c => (c, r.get c)
    73	
    74	/-- The first unique key (in order) on which another row (not `except`)
    75	collides with `img`. Keys with a null component never collide (a nullable
    76	unique key permits tied nulls; indexes card). -/
    77	def findClash (rows : List Row) (keys : List (List String)) (img : Row) (except : Option (List Nat)) :
    78	    Option (Nat × Row) :=
    79	  let rec go (i : Nat) : List (List String) → Option (Nat × Row)
    80	    | [] => none
    81	    | k :: ks =>
    82	      let kv := keyOf k img
    83	      if kv.any (·.2 == .null) then go (i + 1) ks
    84	      else match rows.find? (fun r => keyMatch kv r && except != some r.id) with
    85	        | some r => some (i, r)
    86	        | none => go (i + 1) ks
    87	  go 0 keys
    88	
    89	/-- The refusal for a visible clash on unique key `i` of `["id"] ++ uniques`
    90	(`withId`) or of `uniques`. -/
    91	def clashCode (td : TableDecl) (withId : Bool) (i : Nat) : Stop :=
    92	  let j := if withId then i - 1 else i
    93	  if withId && i = 0 then .refuse "E_CONSTRAINT"
    94	  else match td.uniqueCodes[j]? with
    95	    | some (some code) => .refuse code
    96	    | _ => .refuse "E_UNIQUE"
    97	
    98	def findRow (rows : List Row) (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
    99	  if ks.any (·.2 == .null) then none else rows.find? (keyMatch ks)
   100	
   101	/-- The result of a write: the row if the viewer can read it afterwards,
   102	else null (`why E_CONFLICT`: results are read-rule gets; OPEN W4 for insert). -/
   103	def resultOf (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
   104	  if readable sch s v t r then r.toValue else .null
   105	
   106	def resultOfAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
   107	    (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
   108	  if readableAt sch s v now t r then r.toValue else .null
   109	
   110	/-- `guardE b e` continues when `b` holds and refuses `e` otherwise. -/
   111	def guardE (b : Bool) (e : Stop) : Except Stop Unit := if b then .ok () else .error e
   112	
   113	def doInsertImage (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   114	    (img : Row) (ifAbsent : Bool) (clashHidden : Stop) :
   115	    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
   116	  -- Insert authority has already been checked. Remaining unique checks and
   117	  -- the physical insertion use the post-retirement store.
   118	  match findClash (s t) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
   119	  | some (i, r) => do
   120	    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) clashHidden
   121	    if ifAbsent then pure (.null, s) else throw (clashCode td true i)
   122	  | none =>
   123	    let s' := s.insertRow t img
   124	    pure (resultOfAt sch s' v now t img, s')
   125	
   126	/-- An update's `if` condition: `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable target,
   127	`E_CONFLICT` when false. -/
   128	def condCheck (rd : Bool) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) (old : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
   129	  match cond with
   130	  | some f => do
   131	    guardE rd notFound
   132	    let b ← f old
   133	    guardE b (.refuse "E_CONFLICT")
   134	  | none => pure ()
   135	
   136	/-- A secondary unique clash of an update's next image with another row. -/
   137	def clashCheck (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   138	    (rd : Bool) (old nw : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
   139	  match findClash (s t) td.uniques nw (some old.id) with
   140	  | some (i, r) =>
   141	    throw (if !rd then notFound else if !(readableAt sch s v now t r) then eRule else clashCode td false i)
   142	  | none => pure ()
   143	
   144	def doUpdateRow (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   145	    (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) :
   146	    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
   147	  let nw ← patchImage td old patch
   148	  guardE (td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw })

   150	  condCheck (readableAt sch s v now t old) cond old
   151	  clashCheck sch s v now t td (readableAt sch s v now t old) old nw
   152	  pure (resultOfAt sch (s.replaceRow t old nw) v now t nw, s.replaceRow t old nw)
   153	
   154	/-- The id of an absent upsert's new row: from the key, else the patch. -/
   155	def upsertId (ks ps : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop (List Nat) :=
   156	  match ks.lookup "id" with
   157	  | some (.id x) => pure x
   158	  | _ => match ps.lookup "id" with
   159	    | some (.id x) => pure x
   160	    | _ => throw eInput
   161	
   162	def insertId (fs : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop (List Nat) :=
   163	  match fs.lookup "id" with
   164	  | some (.id x) => pure x
   165	  | _ => throw eInput
   166	
   167	/-! ## Referential actions (LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
   168	
   169	/-- Every reference that names table `t` and carries an action:
   170	`(child table, column, action)`. -/
   171	def referencing (sch : Schema) (t : String) : List (String × String × OnDelete) :=
   172	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => td.cols.filterMap fun c =>
   173	    match c.ref, c.onDelete with
   174	    | some p, some a => if p == t then some (td.name, c.name, a) else none
   175	    | _, _ => none
   176	
   177	/-- Row `k` names the row with id `i` through column `c`. -/
   178	def names (k : Row) (c : String) (i : List Nat) : Bool := k.get c == .id i
   179	
   180	def inClosure (cl : List (String × Row)) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   181	  cl.any fun p => p.1 == t && p.2.id == r.id
   182	
   183	/-- The rows one step of cascades reaches from `(t, r)`. -/
   184	def cascadeKids (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : List (String × Row) :=
   185	  (referencing sch t).flatMap fun (c, col, a) =>
   186	    if a == .cascade then ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id).map fun k => (c, k) else []
   187	
   188	/-- Breadth-first closure over `cascade` references, each row once; `fuel`
   189	bounds the walk (the store's row count suffices). -/
   190	def closure (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row)
   191	  | 0, _, acc => acc
   192	  | _ + 1, [], acc => acc
   193	  | f + 1, (t, r) :: rest, acc =>
   194	    let new := (cascadeKids sch s t r).foldl (fun n p => if inClosure (acc ++ n) p.1 p.2 then n else n ++ [p]) []
   195	    closure sch s f (rest ++ new) (acc ++ new)
   196	
   197	/-- Some `restrict` reference names a closure row from outside the closure. -/
   198	def restricted (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (cl : List (String × Row)) : Bool :=
   199	  cl.any fun (t, r) => (referencing sch t).any fun (c, col, a) =>
   200	    a == .restrict && (s c).any fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k
   201	
   202	def clearCol (r : Row) (c : String) : Row :=
   203	  { r with cols := r.cols.map fun p => if p.1 == c then (p.1, Scalar.null) else p }
   204	
   205	/-- Clear every `set null` reference that names a closure row from outside it. -/
   206	def setNulls (sch : Schema) (cl : List (String × Row)) (s : Store) : Store :=
   207	  cl.foldl (fun s (t, r) => (referencing sch t).foldl (fun s (c, col, a) =>
   208	    if a == .setNull then
   209	      ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k).foldl
   210	        (fun s k => s.replaceRow c k (clearCol k col)) s
   211	    else s) s) s
   212	
   213	def storeSize (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat := sch.tables.foldl (fun n td => n + (s td.name).length) 0
   214	
   215	/-- The store after deleting `old` from `t` with its referential actions, or
   216	`E_REFERENCED`. With no action-carrying reference into `t`, exactly
   217	`removeRow` (LLP 3000.039 §1). -/
   218	def refDelete (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
   219	  let cl := closure sch s (storeSize sch s + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
   220	  if restricted sch s cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
   221	  else pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) (setNulls sch cl s))
   222	
   223	/-- Apply actions to the physical store using only the rows that are logically
   224	live as action witnesses. The root may itself be absent from `witnesses`. -/
   225	def refDeleteFrom (sch : Schema) (witnesses physical : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
   226	  let cl := closure sch witnesses (storeSize sch witnesses + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
   227	  if restricted sch witnesses cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
   228	  else
   229	    let physical := cl.foldl (fun s (parent, row) => (referencing sch parent).foldl (fun s (child, col, action) =>
   230	      if action == .setNull then
   231	        ((witnesses child).filter fun k => names k col row.id && !inClosure cl child k).foldl
   232	          (fun s witness => match (s child).find? fun current => current.id == witness.id with
   233	            | some current =>
   234	              if names current col row.id then s.replaceRow child current (clearCol current col) else s
   235	            | none => s) s
   236	      else s) s) physical
   237	    pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) physical)
   238	
   239	/-! ## Expiry retirement (LLP 3000.036.003 §6; LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
   240	
   241	def expired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   242	  match td.expire with
   243	  | none => false
   244	  | some c => match r.get c with
   245	    | .int closes => closes <= now
   246	    | _ => false
   247	
   248	def stored (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   249	  (s t).any fun current => current.id == r.id
   250	
   251	/-- Retire a due row that physically holds an inserted id. The native engine
   252	does this before checking the new image's remaining unique keys, in the same
   253	transaction as the insert. -/
   254	def retireExpiredSameId (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) (t : String)
   255	    (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) : Except Stop Store :=
   256	  match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
   257	  | some old =>
   258	    if expired td now old then refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old
   259	    else pure s
   260	  | none => pure s
   261	
   262	/-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
   263	stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
   264	model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
   265	root can be retired immediately. -/
   266	def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
   267	  sch.tables.foldl (fun s td => (s td.name).foldl (fun s r =>
   268	    if expired td now r && stored s td.name r then
   269	      match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s td.name r with
   270	      | .ok next => next
   271	      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => s
   272	      | .error _ => s
   273	    else s) s) s
   274	
   275	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — same-id replacement authorizes, retires with actions, then inserts.
   276	/-- Apply one write to the store. -/
   277	def applyWrite (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Except Stop (Value × Store)
   278	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent =>
   279	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   280	    | none => throw eInput
   281	    | some td => do
   282	      let fs ← scalarsE fields
   283	      let rid ← insertId fs
   284	      let img ← buildImage td rid fs eInput

   286	      -- predecessor is still present, then retires it and applies its actions.
   287	      guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) eRule
   288	      let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   289	      doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img ifAbsent eRule

   291	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   292	    | none => throw eInput
   293	    | some td => do
   294	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   295	      let ps ← scalarsE patch

   297	      | none => throw notFound
   298	      | some old => do
   299	        guardE (unexpired td cx.now old) notFound
   300	        doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps cond
   301	  | .upsert t key patch =>
   302	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   303	    | none => throw eInput
   304	    | some td => do
   305	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   306	      let ps ← scalarsE patch
   307	      match findRow ((s t).filter (unexpired td cx.now)) ks with
   308	      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps none
   309	      | none => do
   310	        let rid ← upsertId ks ps
   311	        let img ← buildImage td rid (ks ++ ps) notFound
   312	        guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) notFound
   313	        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   314	        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img false notFound
   315	  | .delete t key =>
   316	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   317	    | none => throw eInput
   318	    | some td => do
   319	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   320	      match findRow (s t) ks with
   321	      | none => throw notFound
   322	      | some old => do
   323	        guardE (unexpired td cx.now old) notFound
   324	        guardE (td.delete.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some old })

   329	end Quarry
   315	}

I found two material gaps: row-keyed-view sources can still be deleted on expiry through a raw store path that skips reference actions, and Lean’s unique-key checks treat other expired rows as collisions while runtime releases those keys. I’m checking the exact line references and supported shapes before returning the findings.

   264	
   265	An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
   266	logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
   267	store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
   268	`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its

   270	
   271	**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes

codex
NOT READY

1. **Row-keyed-view sources bypass expiry reference actions.** [write.rs:942](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write.rs:942) deletes an expired source directly through `tx.delete`. Updating a live source row to expire now therefore removes it despite a live restrict child, and skips cascade/set-null actions. Commit-end retirement cannot repair this because the row is already absent. This violates P1’s transactional retirement contract.

2. **Lean incorrectly treats expired secondary-key occupants as collisions.** [Write.lean:118](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean:118) and [Write.lean:139](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean:139) search the entire physical store. With an unswept expired row holding a unique `tag`, inserting another id with that tag produces `E_RULE` in Lean; runtime releases the key through [write.rs:756](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write.rs:756) and admits the insert. This is inside the supported expiry fragment.

3. **Lean’s `insert if absent` can commit retirement during a runtime no-op.** [Write.lean:288](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean:288) retires an expired same-id predecessor before checking remaining unique collisions. If another live row occupies the proposed secondary key, Lean returns a no-op after deleting the predecessor and cascading its children. Runtime returns `false` before retirement at [write.rs:147](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write.rs:147), preserving those rows.
